sessions.description: The place matters as much as the ideas it holds. Opening Wave 2026 from the heart of the venue itself, this keynote reflects on the role that cities and platforms like OGR Torino can play in connecting innovation, culture, business, research and talent. In a moment shaped by the rapid rise of AI, the sustainable transition and the growing interdependence between sectors and geographies, the real question is not only which technologies will drive change, but who will know how to steer it and turn it into shared value. Drawing on the transformation of OGR and of Turin itself, it makes the case for new alliances between local and international ecosystems, between technology and cultural production, between competitiveness and responsibility to a place, and for a model where a hub becomes the infrastructure that brings together skills, capital, companies, talent and communities, opening a local story to the world.

sessions.title: Tactical AI: how to save 15 minutes every hour
sessions.description:
Every few months a new AI tool reshapes the landscape, and teams that went all-in on the previous one find themselves starting over. This masterclass introduces a robust, tool-agnostic approach to integrating AI into daily operations — one that delivers measurable time savings today without creating fragile dependencies on any single platform.

Participants will work through a hands-on framework for evaluating AI tools tactically: which tasks to delegate, how to structure prompts for repeatable results, and how to design workflows that survive the next disruption. The goal is practical: walk out with a personal AI playbook you can use Monday morning, regardless of which tool you're using six months from now.

sessions.title: The Sovereignty Stack: Cyber-resilience in the Age of Frontier AI
sessions.description:
Frontier AI fundamentally redraws the cybersecurity landscape by giving attackers exponential leverage: automated vulnerability discovery, adaptive social engineering, and models built to evade detection. Defenders, meanwhile, stay trapped within linear constraints like budget cycles, talent shortages, and legacy infrastructure.

This imbalance shifts cyber-resilience from a purely technical problem into a core issue of technological sovereignty. In an era where the most capable AI systems belong to a handful of jurisdictions, whoever controls the models, compute, and training pipelines ultimately holds the strategic advantage.

Building true defense requires mastering the sovereignty stack across every layer, from chip architecture and model governance to real-time incident response. Closing sovereignty gaps by reducing strategic dependencies and investing in native AI capabilities is the only way forward. Cyber-resilience can no longer be a passive compliance checkbox, but must become a central geopolitical asset.

sessions.title: How Prediction Markets Are Changing the Way We See the World
sessions.description: For centuries, we trusted polls, experts, and mainstream media to tell us what the world thinks. One guest built a different approach. Trained as a professional ballerina before turning to mathematics and computer science, she co-founded a platform that lets people trade directly on the probability of real-world events, and when regulators tried to prevent election markets from running on Kalshi, she chose to sue the U.S. government rather than back down. She won, in a ruling that made legal, federally regulated election markets possible in America for the first time in over a century. Weekly trading volume on the platform she built now exceeds a billion dollars, and her company is valued at over $22 billion. She's joined on stage by one of Italy's most followed independent voices in tech and entrepreneurship, built entirely outside traditional media gatekeepers, for a conversation on what happens to trust and truth when both money and attention move outside the institutions that used to hold them.

sessions.title: Fuel for life: food, wellbeing and the case for innovation

sessions.title: Rewriting the Rules: From the Open Web to the Age of AI

sessions.title: The ecosystem builders: two women leading the way
sessions.description: Diyala D'Aveni is the reason Vento and Wave itself exist: the conviction that Italy's entrepreneurial talent deserves a real ecosystem, not just capital. Donatella Sciuto has spent her career building the institution that trains the engineers and researchers behind that talent. Together, they discuss what it actually takes to build an ecosystem that lasts and why more women need to be doing the building.

sessions.title: How to build a self-updating Knowledge Base: integrating code, AI, and business processes
sessions.description:
Documentation goes stale the day after it's written, and every question ends up in engineering's inbox. At Serenis we stopped writing docs and started producing sources a pipeline can read: a wiki on product and processes that updates itself from code and internal tools, with metadata deciding who sees what. The same knowledge base serves people and AI agents alike: it powers our patient-facing assistants and lets other teams (sales, marketing, ops etc.) ask questions in plain language. We'll show how we redesigned the way we write code, tickets and decisions to make this work, how a human review gate keeps hallucinations out, and what still doesn't update itself.

sessions.title: One Agent per Person: lessons from building OpenClaw at scale
sessions.description:
A personal AI agent is only useful if it actually knows you — your history, your preferences, your way of working. That promise is easy to deliver for ten users. At ten thousand, it becomes a genuinely hard problem.
ROSS is our answer to that challenge: a personal AI assistant, available on Telegram, that connects to each user's tools and acts on their behalf. Building ROSS taught us that the hardest part of scaling a personal agent is not making it smart. It is keeping it genuinely personal as the user base grows: maintaining coherent per-user context across sessions, managing the tension between personalization depth and operational cost, and making sure the agent that serves user number 9,847 feels as personal as the one that served user number one.
This talk shares what we learned building ROSS at NextMindLab — where the architecture breaks, what tradeoffs are unavoidable, and what a production personal agent actually looks like under the hood.

sessions.title: From Models to Production: exploring the Enterprise AI stack
sessions.description:
AI models are becoming more capable, while the cost of a given level of capability continues to fall. Yet moving AI from experimentation to production raises questions of reliability, control, observability and cost. The model is only one component of the architecture enterprises need to operate AI in production. This masterclass examines that architecture through three economic functions: Capability Cost, the cost of accessing the required intelligence; Coordination Cost, the cost of combining models, data and tools; and Execution Cost, the cost of making outputs usable at the required level of assurance. It also considers the factors that may determine whether the software functions supporting these needs remain independent or are integrated into model, cloud or application platforms.

sessions.title: Steve Jobs, the Untold Chapter
sessions.description:

Pushed out of the company he founded, Steve Jobs spent over a decade building ventures the world had written off, a period of spectacular failures that quietly forged the leader who would go on to reshape technology and culture forever. The book Steve Jobs in Exile reconstructs those forgotten years, and this conversation revisits them with its author alongside an executive who worked with Jobs during his return to Apple and helped drive the comeback from the inside. Together they explore what that crucible reveals about vision, resilience, and the making of the products that define how we live today.

The company now moves hundreds of billions of dollars a year and was recently valued in the double-digit billions, built by a founder who turned down a billion-dollar acquisition offer because he wasn't done building yet. Together they explore what China actually brings to the table on AI, how that differs from the dominant American narrative, and how one of the world's largest companies is building cloud and intelligence from the ground up. sessions.description: If the last conversation was about opening software creation to everyone, this one asks the opposite question: what happens to the experts? Inside the world's largest engineering teams, a different shift is underway, one where seasoned developers hand entire workflows to autonomous agents that test, debug, migrate, and increasingly decide. The frontier here is not accessibility but trust: how much of the work can a machine truly own, and what does it take for a Fortune 500 to bet its codebase on one. A look at the professional edge of the agentic era, where autonomy is measured not in who can build, but in how little a human needs to touch.

sessions.description: As AI leaves the screen and enters the physical world, industry, infrastructure and buildings become the stage where intelligence delivers measurable value

sessions.title: From Minds to Matter
sessions.description: This is the moment the conversation turns from intelligence that lives on screens to intelligence that reshapes the physical world. On one side, the frontier models learning to reason their way through problems once thought to require human insight. On the other, AI systems discovering the materials that could capture carbon, power batteries, and fuel cleaner flight. Together they trace the same arc: artificial intelligence moving from generating words and code to designing the stuff the world is actually made of. A conversation about what happens when the most advanced AI stops describing reality and starts engineering it.

sessions.title: Innovation at industrial scale
sessions.description: Critical infrastructure, shipbuilding, defense, this conversation brings together different perspectives on what it actually takes to fund and construct technology at that scale.

sessions.title: Embodied Intelligence: A New Era Begins
sessions.description: AI has learned to reason. Now it is learning to act. A NASA alumnus, Stanford professor, and Vice President at NVIDIA leading autonomous systems and Physical AI research, Marco Pavone traces the arc from early autonomous systems to today's physical AI revolution—from planetary rovers to autonomous vehicles to the next generation of embodied intelligence. Drawing on his experience spanning academia and industry, he offers a clear-eyed perspective on where we are, how we got here, and what the convergence of AI, robotics, and the physical world means for industry, society, and the future of human work. This keynote opens Wave's robotics session with a forward-looking view of the opportunities and challenges shaping the next era of Physical AI.

sessions.title: Evolution or Revolution? Why AI Advantage belongs to leaders who move smart
sessions.description:
The AI honeymoon is over. Senior leaders are no longer asked whether AI can work; they are being asked why it is not yet changing cost, speed, CX, and growth. The choice now is sharper: where to pursue Evolution, using AI to strengthen existing models, and where Revolution is required, rebuilding workflows around AI execution.

Led by Dave Pattman (VP of Transformation, Concentrix EMEA) and Davide Tinelli (COO, Concentrix Italy), this masterclass challenges leaders to confront the gap between AI activity and AI advantage. It will expose where value leaks, why proof-of-concepts fail to scale, and how fragmented programmes become a liability as competitors redesign how work gets done.

This is not about chasing every use case. It is about moving smart: knowing when to optimise, when to reinvent, and how to scale AI with the governance, data, orchestration, and accountability needed to create measurable business impact before the market forces the agenda.

sessions.title: Scaling into Europe: 10 years of lessons from ICEX’s Rising Up in Spain program
sessions.description:
Over the past decade, ICEX has supported hundreds of startups and scaleups in their international growth journey through Rising Up in Spain, its flagship soft-landing program for foreign entrepreneurs. Drawing on 10 years of experience, this masterclass will explore the key challenges startups face when scaling internationally, the common success factors behind sustainable growth, and how Spain can serve as a strategic gateway to European markets. The session is designed for startup founders, scaleup executives, innovation leaders, and international entrepreneurs looking to expand their business and accelerate growth in Europe.
AI is not dying. The era of infinite scaling is. The next generation of AI will be judged by its ability to operate in the real world, generate trust and create measurable impact for people.
Drawing on AgorAI's experience, this lecture examines the principles shaping the next wave of AI. From distributed and multi-agent architectures to compute minimization, Physical AI, Digital Twins, Decision Intelligence and AI Security, the focus shifts from building increasingly powerful models to designing systems that are useful, explainable and accountable by design.
Through real-world challenges and emerging architectures, the session outlines a path beyond the race for larger models toward AI that augments human capabilities and delivers meaningful impact across mobility, agriculture, healthcare, critical infrastructure and security.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: The business of longevity
sessions.description: A conversation on what it takes to turn the science of aging into treatments and investments that actually reach people

sessions.title: When AI Hits the Road
sessions.description: Until now, the intelligence on stage has lived inside screens and codebases. Here it steps into the physical world in the most demanding way imaginable: two tons of metal moving through live traffic, with no one behind the wheel. Autonomous driving is the ultimate test of physical AI, where a mistake is measured not in a failed output but in the real world, and where perception, prediction, and decision-making have to work flawlessly millions of times a day. This conversation goes inside the long road to autonomy, the breakthroughs that finally made driverless vehicles real, and what it takes to earn the public's trust in machines that move us.

sessions.title: From Space to the Factory Floor: The Rise of Physical AI
sessions.description:
We started in research - at DLR, the German Aerospace Center, one of Europe's leading institutes for space robotics. Machines built for places no human could reach: orbiting a space station, reaching toward a comet. Out there, precision isn't optional.
That work raised a harder question. Language models had learned to write and reason, but intelligence that never touches anything is only half an intelligence. The real frontier isn't what a machine can say. It's what it can do. Today we call this Physical AI.
Answering that question meant leaving the lab. We founded Agile Robots to bring what we'd learned in aerospace to the factory floor. Today our robots work alongside people - assembling electronics, watching over production lines, standing in operating rooms.
This keynote takes a visionary look ahead - at what Physical AI makes possible next, and at the industries and everyday moments it will eventually reach: Space taught precision. The factory floor is teaching scale.

sessions.title: Inside the operating room of the future - from robots to data
sessions.description: Intuitive Surgical is the company behind the pioneering da Vinci surgical system, which has transformed how millions of patients globally experience surgery. By combining robotics, imaging and digital intelligence, Intuitive is shaping a future where procedures are less invasive, recovery is faster and surgeons are empowered like never before. Come to this session if you want to hear about how this revolution began, where it's headed and what it means for the future of healthcare.

sessions.title: The hybrid shopper and the rise of agentic commerce
sessions.description: Today's shoppers move between app, website and store without thinking about it, buying in-store through an app or arriving with a decision already made alongside an AI assistant. This hybrid behaviour is changing what retailers need: connected channels, a single experience from first touch to purchase, and a new kind of visibility, because being found and being chosen increasingly happens inside a language model. The next step is agentic commerce, where AI agents take the customer from choice to payment. Nexi and CommerceClarity and Veliu discuss how retail is adapting and what it takes to be ready.

sessions.title: Physical AI & Robotics: the next industrial revolution
sessions.description:
Artificial intelligence is leaving the screen and entering the physical world. Humanoid robots — machines that move, reason, and collaborate in human environments — are no longer a science fiction concept: they represent a $160 billion market by 2035, fuelled by an aging workforce, collapsing unit costs, and an acceleration of AI capabilities that no previous automation cycle has matched. This masterclass, led by Bain & Company, takes participants from the macro forces driving the Physical AI revolution to the competitive landscape taking shape today, and closes with concrete strategic moves that companies, investors, and innovators should be making right now. Data-driven, provocative, and grounded in real client work across Europe and beyond.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Connecting Ecosystems: the UK’s role in powering international innovation
sessions.description:
The UK has long been recognised as one of the world’s leading innovation ecosystems, combining world-class talent, capital, research and international connectivity. But what does it take to turn innovation into scalable global growth? This conversation will explore how the UK supports businesses at every stage of their international journey, from attracting investment and fostering entrepreneurship to helping companies expand into new markets. It will also examine how governments, cities and innovation partners can work together to strengthen international collaboration and unlock new opportunities in an increasingly competitive global economy.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Venture Europe
How to Reindustrialize Europe in 10 Minutes or Less
sessions.description: Europe builds some of the best machines in the world. Now, advances in robotics and AI are opening up new possibilities for what we can build, where we can build it, and what can scale. Drawing on a front-row seat backing founders reinventing everything from factories to farming and working in Brussels on the most ambitious policy projects, this session makes the case for a Europe that does not set out to catch up, but to win. This almost heretical closing keynote challenges the received wisdom about European manufacturing and lays out what it will take to turn industrial strength into global leadership: building machines, building factories, abundant energy, a unified market, capital that lets ambition scale, and a new generation of founders that builds GDP-driving companies. A practical, impatiently optimistic argument for Europe’s industrial future – and how we can get on with building it.

sessions.title: Soil: where biology, technology, and productivity converge
sessions.description: Bioinspired robotics, applied biology, and next-generation agricultural machinery come together to explore how innovation can protect soil health while advancing productivity and long-term farm sustainability

sessions.title: The State of the European Tech Ecosystem
sessions.description: The session opens with a wide-angle view of European tech today, grounded in data. A look at where the ecosystem stands right now, the forces shaping its trajectory, and the signals worth paying attention to as the year unfolds. From funding and growth to the structural shifts redefining how and where companies get built, this keynote sets out the landscape before the conversation turns to what it all means. The starting point for everything that follows

sessions.title: The Revenue You Can’t See: a full-field framework to unlock hidden B2B pipeline with AI, data, and channels
sessions.description:
A workshop for people responsible for growth, pipeline and revenue who want to see the full playing field.
There are far more ways to understand a buyer, reach an account, create familiarity, spot opportunity and move a deal than most teams are taught.
Over 45 minutes, we’ll unpack some of the most underused ideas across sales, research, public data, channels, demand generation and AI, and show how they fit together around one commercial goal: creating more opportunities to win.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: The Vibe Coding Era: why the next billion builders won't write a single line of code with Replit
sessions.description:
AI hasn't just changed how software gets built, it's changed who gets to build it. In this 45 minutes hands-on masterclass, you'll use Replit to go from a blank prompt to a working, deployed app, live. No setup. No prior experience. Just bring an idea and leave with something real.

sessions.title: Founded & Grounded
The Compounding Bet
sessions.description: Every session today has asked some version of the same question: can Europe build companies that define a category rather than follow one. This closing conversation answers it directly, through the relationship between an investor who bet early on a founder still in his twenties and the company he built into the continent's most valuable legal AI platform in under three years. What began as an outsider's attempt to crack one of the most change-resistant industries in the world became a global expansion machine, growing the team tenfold in a single year and winning firms across dozens of jurisdictions that had already been burned by AI once before. A conversation between the builder and the backer who saw it coming, on what it actually takes to compound conviction into a category leader, and why the next decade of European tech may be decided by exactly this kind of bet.

sessions.title: CEO interview: how companies avoid losing the trillion-dollar AI bet

sessions.title: Building Deep Tech in Europe
sessions.description: European tech is often caricatured as software and services, yet some of the continent's most ambitious companies are being built at the hard edges of science and engineering. This keynote looks at what it takes to build category-defining deep tech from Europe and compete globally from day one: navigating capital, talent, and regulation while taking on incumbents many times your size. A first-hand perspective on turning European scientific strength into companies that matter on the world stage.

sessions.title: The line AI can't cross
sessions.description: AI no longer just answers, it decides, prices, and acts across entire business processes. A cross-industry researcher and an insurance leader compare notes on where the machine should lead, and where a human still needs to hold the line

sessions.title: Where Europe's Next Founders Come From
sessions.description: Talent is the raw material of every tech ecosystem, and Europe has never been short of it. This session pairs a ground-level view of the continent's emerging builders with the perspective of a global investor who has backed companies across cycles and geographies. Together they ask where the next generation of European founders is actually being formed, what's pulling them toward ambition rather than caution, and what the ecosystem still needs to give them to build at global scale. A bottom-up and top-down read on Europe's most important asset: its people.

sessions.title: From AI Theatre to P&L Impact: how to rewire software business models AI-first
sessions.description:
Everyone is talking about AI, yet few are seeing it show up in the numbers. Hg is Europe's largest tech investor actively deploying AI at scale across its portfolio of c.60 tech and services businesses - with 1,600+ live AI projects, over 150 AI FDEs, showing c.$260m of P&L impact. This session, led by Chris Kindt (Partner and Head of AI Value Creation, Hg) and Tim Harrison (AI Team Lead, Hg), cuts through the hype to show what genuinely drives financial impact, and how to deliver the ‘AI-first rewiring’ needed to deliver sustained value. We'll share a practical framework and our ‘lessons learnt’ for AI-led transformation, illustrated with first-hand case studies from Hg-backed companies, and leave founders with concrete advice they can apply immediately. It's a hands-on session for founders and operators who want to move from AI pilots to measurable business impact.

sessions.title: Boost your business. Build your internal tools with AI, without writing code
sessions.description:
Information scattered across shared folders, Excel sheets and emails, tasks assigned
over WhatsApp, procedures that exist only in the head of whoever has been doing them for
years. If you run an SME, you know exactly how much these compromises cost in terms of
time and errors. In this masterclass we will see how AI has made something new possible:
building internal digital tools, tailored to your own processes, without the need for a technical
team. Starting from a real case, we will cover every phase of the journey: mapping
processes, defining requirements, building with AI and going live. Practical, concrete,
designed for whoever runs a business and wants it to work better.

sessions.title: Chapeau Media
Who trains the trains
sessions.description: A play on the double meaning: institutional strategy trains the system, and engineering trains the physical trains. The conversation focuses on the gap between designing an AI doctrine for Italian industry and actually deploying it inside a live rail network, where every model must answer to physics, not just policy.

sessions.title: European Capital, Global Bets
sessions.description: Not every story about Europe and global tech starts with a founder leaving the continent to build somewhere else. Sometimes it starts with a European investor staying exactly where he is and still writing the check that all of Silicon Valley wanted. This fireside follows a London-based growth partner who moved fast enough to preempt one of the most competitive enterprise AI rounds of the past year, backing a founder who took on a two-decade-old category leader and rebuilt it from scratch in about a year, using AI agents to automate the work an entire industry assumed only humans could own. A conversation about competing for the best deals in the world without needing to sit in the room where they happen, and what that says about where conviction is increasingly based.

sessions.title: From Italian capital to European scale
sessions.description: Italy has built the capital to grow startups at home. The next test is growing the founders who can take them further. CDP Venture Capital and ICE discuss how funding and international markets can work as one path, and what it takes to raise a new generation of young entrepreneurs who think European from day one.

sessions.title: The Model Europe Built
sessions.description: The AI everyone talks about was built to handle words and images. But the data that actually runs the world's businesses, the rows and columns inside every financial record, supply chain, and customer database, has stayed stubbornly out of reach, because general-purpose models barely understand tables and numbers at all. In this fireside chat, the Chief Technology Officer of one of Europe's largest software companies makes the case for tabular foundation models as a genuinely new category of AI. The evidence: Prior Labs, the European research team that built the world's most advanced one – and a commitment of over a billion euros to turn that academic breakthrough into a world-leading frontier AI lab on European soil. It's a rare look at one of the year's most significant European AI deals: what it takes to identify and back a foundation model that beats the giants at something they overlooked, why a European enterprise champion decided to bet on it rather than import intelligence from elsewhere, and what this partnership says about whether Europe can build and keep frontier AI of its own.

sessions.title: H.A.R. Orchestration: The Framework for Scaling AI into Competitive Advantage
sessions.description:
Scaling in 2026 is no longer about adding headcount, it’s about amplifying human potential through architectural synergy. In this executive masterclass, Simone Enea Riccò unveils the H.A.R. Framework (Humans, Agents, Robots). As Frontier AI redefines the boundaries of the possible, the real competitive advantage lies in orchestration. Learn how to strategically integrate Human Judgment with Agentic AI Processes and Physical Automation. This is the definitive roadmap for C-level leaders to transform technological complexity into a unified, high-performance ecosystem where AI doesn't replace talent, it unleashes it.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: The end of the SaaS gold rush: what to sell when AI does everything?
sessions.description:
As AI commodities traditional software, standard SaaS features are no longer enough to win. This hands-on session goes beyond theory to give you an actionable playbook for building defensible value when execution costs fall to zero.

Mathieu Nebra, founder of OpenClassrooms (the leading online education platform in Europe), will help us identify what stays valuable when software alone isn't enough. Inspired by the popular issue What to sell if AI does everything?, this workshop will audit your current positioning and map out concrete strategies to pivot towards high-margin assets, including proprietary data networks, trust-based distribution, real-world execution, and high-stakes accountability. Leave with a clear framework to adapt your business model and lead in an AI-first market.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Startup Europe - The Sifted Podcast
The Category Makers
sessions.description: For twenty years, being found online meant one thing: ranking on a search engine. That world is quietly ending. As people increasingly ask AI instead of searching, a company's reputation is being written by models most brands can't see, let alone shape. This conversation brings together the founder building the tools to understand and influence how brands show up inside AI answers, and the investor who backed the idea before the category even had a name. It's a look at what it takes to create a market rather than compete in one: how you sell a product for a problem companies don't yet know they have, why the biggest opportunities are the ones that are invisible until they're obvious, and what the end of search means for every business that has spent two decades optimizing for it. A conversation about seeing the future early, and building the company that defines it.

sessions.title: The Power of Proximity
sessions.description: In a world where AI can be built and accessed from anywhere, it would be easy to assume that where you are no longer matters. The opposite is turning out to be true. Europe's most important startup hubs have become dense, physical communities, places where founders, researchers, investors and the AI companies backing them all work side by side, and that closeness is producing some of the continent's most significant companies. This conversation brings together the person who runs one of the world's largest homes for startups and a leader from one of the AI companies partnering with that ecosystem to support its founders. Together they explore why geography still shapes innovation, what actually turns a place into a magnet for talent and ambition, and why, even in the age of borderless technology, the proximity of people building together may matter more than ever.

sessions.title: Where Conviction Goes
sessions.description: Two investors, two completely different bets, the same underlying instinct: back the founder's obsession before the market spreadsheet agrees. One moved fast enough to close a term sheet in hours for a consumer AI breakout. One has spent a career finding founders the traditional map overlooks entirely. This conversation isn't about who moves faster, it's about where conviction lands when it does, and what that reveals about which bets actually compound over a decade.

sessions.title: Don't kill your deal: surviving the Deadly Sins of Fundraising
sessions.description:
Why do some startups secure funding while others lose momentum before reaching the finish line? Which tools can supercharge your financing? How do you choose the right investor mix for your fundraising round and long-term strategy? This hands-on masterclass combines expert insights with interactive decision-making to uncover the main fundraising mistakes founders make most often. Participants will be challenged with real-world scenarios, discuss the best course of action, and compare their choices with the perspective of investors and fundraising experts.
A practical session for founders, innovators and startup teams looking to sharpen their fundraising strategy, avoid costly missteps and increase their chances of turning investor conversations into meaningful partnerships. The session will be hosted by Marta Casassa, Innovation Lab Manager for Opening Future, a joint project by Google Cloud, Intesa Sanpaolo, and TIM Enterprise, and Niccolò Sanarico, Partner and CTO at Primo Capital.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: From Speculation to Infrastructure: how blockchain is entering the banking system
sessions.description:
For years, blockchain was associated mainly with cryptocurrencies and speculation. More recently, that picture has begun to change: banks and financial institutions are using the technology to move money and financial assets faster, around the clock and with greater automation. This session will explore how blockchain is becoming part of the infrastructure behind payments and financial markets, what is already happening in practice, and what still needs to change before it can be adopted at scale.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Automating the Unglamorous
sessions.description: Long before AI agents became the phrase on every stage, a founder in Dublin was quietly building software that does the work no one wants to talk about: the repetitive, high-stakes tasks that keep security and IT teams up at night. No hype, no consumer flash, just automation for the parts of the enterprise that break when they fail. This fireside brings him together with the investor who backed the company early and has stayed close ever since, for a conversation about building a category-defining company from Europe rather than Silicon Valley, why the least glamorous problems often make the most durable businesses, and what changes now that the rest of the world has finally caught up to the idea that software should act, not just assist. A story about conviction, patience, and the quiet advantage of solving a problem years before it became fashionable.

sessions.title: The Operating System of Growth
sessions.description: Behind every fast-scaling company is the invisible machinery that lets it plan, decide, and adapt as conditions shift. This session looks at how a European company built that layer for organizations around the world, and what it reveals about scaling from Europe to global markets. Joined by one of the fast-growing consumer brands that relies on it, the conversation moves from the building of category-defining infrastructure to what growth actually demands on the ground.

sessions.title: Europe's Next Bet
sessions.description: Behind every generation of European champions sits a quiet powerhouse: the institutional capital patient and bold enough to invest before markets will. This conversation is a first, the incoming chief executive of Europe's largest tech investor, taking the stage to set out his vision for the future. He arrives having spent 11 years running a lending business that has delivered over EUR 750bn of policy driven finance, steadily increasing high impact risk investments and building the continent's most important venture debt program from the ground up. Now he doubles down on the critical question: how can Europe finance its own technological independence? Expect a candid look at where public capital can move the needle, the road ahead for the EIB Group’s flagship European Tech Champions initiative and the funds it will back, and what it will really take for Europe to build, fund and keep the companies that define the AI era.

sessions.title: Cleantech: bridging research, policy & capital for industrial scale
sessions.description: As the climate transition intersects with economic security and industrial competitiveness, how can cleantech breakthroughs transition from lab to market? Hosted by OGR Torino, one of Europe’s leading innovation hubs, in collaboration with Cleantech for Italy, the national coalition championing cleantech as a strategic pillar of Italy’s industrial future, this hands-on workshop dives into the mechanics of scaling deep tech innovation. Participants will explore emerging investment trends, high-potential verticals, and the strategic roadmaps needed to navigate the path from research validation to industrial adoption. Through practical insights and ecosystem collaboration, this session offers startups, investors, and innovators actionable strategies to connect policy, capital, and industry—positioning Italy at the forefront of the next generation of industrial innovation.

sessions.title: Everyone talks about AI sovereignty. This masterclass is about how to build it in practice
sessions.description:
Two RedCarbon engineers present a practical sovereign AI blueprint for European founders, addressing the concrete architectural, commercial, and operational trade-offs of building natively in Europe.
Across 40 minutes of presentation, the session breaks down three interconnected layers: the architectural choices governing models, compute, data residency, and engineering locations; the cybersecurity realities of defending sovereign infrastructure against non-sovereign global threats; and the commercial strategy of transforming regulatory frameworks like NIS2, DORA, and the AI Act into a competitive moat with enterprise buyers and MSSP partners.
Attendees will leave with an actionable framework for evaluating sovereignty trade-offs in their own AI product decisions, grounded in the unfiltered engineering and business lessons from a European startup building on home ground by design. The talk concludes with a 5-minute Q&A session.
⚠️ Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Vision-Language Models actually work. just not the way you think
sessions.description:
Everyone is talking about Vision-Language Models. Few organizations are actually using them well. In this session, a CEO and a CTO who have built and shipped VLM systems in production start from the beginning, what these models actually are, why they represent a genuine shift in how machines perceive the world, and why most enterprise implementations miss the point entirely. The conversation moves from first principles to deployment reality: the gap between a model that works on a benchmark and a system that holds up at 3am in a customer's facility, the decisions that actually determine success or failure, and the questions every CTO should be asking before signing off on an AI project. Honest, technical enough to be credible, practical enough to be useful.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: The European Advantage: Building Intelligence at Scale
sessions.description: In the intelligence economy, competitive advantage isn't created by technology alone. It depends on how closely a business can understand, serve and evolve with its customers. In this conversation, the CEO of Visma shares how the company built a European technology champion by taking a different path to scale: combining the reach of a global group with the expertise of local software leaders and the autonomy of entrepreneurs on the ground. She'll also look at what that model means in the age of AI, how a decentralised network turns proximity to hundreds of thousands of customers into an advantage in building AI-era software, where the winners will be those who understand specific needs better than anyone else. From navigating Europe's regulatory complexity to building one of its largest networks of software entrepreneurs, Visma's story offers a perspective on how decentralisation and local intelligence, powered by global scale and long-term ambition, become consistent engines for growth.

sessions.title: SCENARIO: The next fifty years of being human
sessions.description: What happens to a species once it stops being confined to one planet? Tommaso Ghidini opens the day with a keynote on the future of humanity as space exploration accelerates and on what being human might even mean fifty years from now, as bodies, minds, and identity adapt to a life beyond Earth. Less a forecast than an invitation to imagine what comes next, and what is already changing on Earth.

sessions.title: The Whole Board
sessions.description: Most people spend a career on one side of the table. This guest has sat on all of them. He ran one of the world's largest telecoms operators, then stepped into government to lead the country's COVID emergency committee and then the digital transformation at its most critical moment, and now helps deploy global growth capital into the companies shaping the next decade. That rare vantage point, industry, government and investment seen from the inside of each, makes him one of the sharpest voices on the question this session keeps circling: what will it actually take for Europe to compete. Drawing on his work on the Draghi report aimed at turning Europe's competitiveness agenda into action, this conversation looks at where the continent is genuinely falling behind, where its real advantages lie, and why closing the gap is not just about technology but also about the will to innovate, build and scale, supported by courage to change institutional and regulatory frameworks.

sessions.title: Reading the map: where Italian venture stands in Europe
sessions.description: Dealroom tracks every startup, round and exit across Europe. CDP Venture Capital is Italy's largest venture investor. Andrii of Dealroom and Emanuele Levi, CEO of CDP Venture Capital, read the latest data together: how much capital Italian startups raise compared with their European peers, where the gap is widest, and what needs to change for Italy to produce more companies that scale

sessions.title: From Legacy to Leverage: how to orchestrate the largest multi-business AI platforms through a human+machine approach
sessions.description:
Driving high-impact innovation on a blank canvas is hard; doing it across an ecosystem serving millions of customers through one of the largest physical and digital networks in the country is a fundamentally different challenge. Transforming an enterprise that combines fintech, telco, digital identity, and conversational AI demands a brand-new operational playbook. Today, this journey is entering a new phase of acceleration, with the acquisition of TIM representing a potential step-change in scale, capabilities, and platform reach.

In this practical masterclass, we move beyond the hype to examine how legacy assets can be turned into a true competitive edge. Drawing from real-world execution at Poste Italiane, we dissect a hands-on framework for building reusable enterprise AI platforms, orchestrating multi-business touchpoints, and driving deep organizational adoption.

Participants will learn how to combine the structural power of the elephant with the agility of the gazelle. Discover how technology, frontline workflows, and human trust evolve together to scale innovation where it matters most.

sessions.title: From Industrial Cities to Sustainable Urban Futures: planning, governance and participation for urban transformation
sessions.description:
A moderated dialogue between Torino and Kitakyushu, two cities with strong industrial identities that are using
sustainability, innovation, digital transformation and participation to shape new urban development models. The
session combines short city contributions with targeted questions and closes by reflecting on what each city can
learn from the other, using mutual learning as a starting point for more structured future cooperation.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Engineering production agents: the model is the easy part
sessions.description:
Building an impressive agent prototype is increasingly easy. Making it reliable, responsive and economically viable in production is much harder. In this session, Andrea Cunegatti, unpacks that gap through real Nebius Token Factory use cases: how Revolut scaled AI agents across financial crime and customer support, and how Sword Health made a much larger reasoning model responsive enough for its AI wellbeing specialist. The session unfolds those lessons into a practical framework for model choice, inference architecture, observability and cost.
This masterclass is proudly powered by our scaleup partner Nebius.
⚠️ Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Mindset, Not Skillset
sessions.description: What's the 10% of my job the AI will never be able to do?It's the question on everyone's mind, and according to this speaker, it's the wrong one. Think of an expert horse rider learning to drive a car: almost none of the specific riding skills carry over, but the instincts and reflexes underneath them are exactly what make a great driver. The lesson for the AI era is the same. The edge will come from reimagining our roles entirely, exercising judgement rather than clinging to the surface skills. But when it comes to skills being transferred to AIs, and companies relying on skilled Agents to perform their most critical processes, a question arises: how do you ensure that the AI exercises such skills safely, and in a way that protects your intellectual property?Drawing on what it takes to embed AI into the core of one of the world's largest and most complex financial institutions, in this wide-ranging conversation Goldman Sachs' CIO will discuss how the firm is implementing the technology across its businesses, his views on a framework for model safety, and why the hardest and most valuable shift is not learning new tools but building new habits.

sessions.title: The role of telcos in building a sovereign digital ecosystem
sessions.description: n an international landscape marked by growing geopolitical instability and the pervasive centrality of data, technological sovereignty has become a priority at both national and European levels. Amid a transformation accelerated by Artificial Intelligence, securing digital architectures means not only defending digital borders and ensuring the proper functioning of the economy, but also preserving states’ decision-making autonomy. To build a truly sovereign digital ecosystem, it is therefore essential to place telecommunications operators back at the center of Italian and European strategy, the only actors that possess the indispensable critical resources: proprietary fiber and 5G networks, state-of-the-art data centers on national soil, cybersecurity platforms, and expertise. However, to meet this challenge, it will be essential to create the conditions that enable telcos to continue innovating and investing in networks.

sessions.title: Your Knowledge, Your Model
sessions.description: Intelligence is becoming a layer built into the enterprise itself, reshaping how companies design products, run operations, and serve customers. But the next competitive edge won't come from using the same general-purpose models as everyone else. It will come from turning a company's own knowledge, data, and expertise into specialized intelligence, better models for specific domains and specific decisions, rather than simply bigger ones. This keynote reframes the conversation from technology adoption to business architecture: which parts of a company's know-how can be encoded, governed, reused, and scaled, and how the winners will turn AI from an external tool into an internal strategic engine, controllable, adaptable, and deeply aligned with who they are. It's the difference between renting intelligence and owning it.

sessions.title: Beyond the Pilot: How AI Changes the Way Companies Work
sessions.description: AI is moving from individual productivity into the workflows that transform/reimagine the way we run a business. Drawing on what OpenAI is seeing with enterprise customers, this session will explore how leaders turn experimentation into repeatable work: connecting AI to company context and tools, deciding where agents can act, measuring results, and keeping people in control. A practical look at the choices that make intelligence useful across an organization.

sessions.title: From ancient greek to oncology: the case for specialized AI
sessions.description: The conversation around specialised AI will unpack the value of models built around deep domain knowledge. One supports scholars in transcribing and interpreting papyri and inscriptions; another applies clinical and scientific knowledge to support oncology professionals. Two very different fields, one shared bet: AI combining specialised data, governance and a disciplined lifecycle to deliver trustworthy intelligence at scale.

sessions.title: Tech for Humans
sessions.description: For a century, a car did exactly what it was engineered to do, following fixed rules, never more. AI is changing that at the deepest level: the vehicle is evolving beyond moving from programmed behavior, combining engineering excellence with to learned intelligence to create a machine that perceives, reasons and adapts to the world around it. But the point isn't technology for its own sake. It's a driving experience that feels natural and genuinely useful, where people feel the benefit rather than the complexity. This conversation brings together the chief executive of one of the world's largest carmakers, with fourteen automotive brands and global manufacturing reach, and the founder pioneering the AI that lets vehicles learn to drive rather than follow handwritten code. Together they explore what it takes to bring this intelligence to the road responsibly: why the automaker–AI partnership can move faster than either side alone, how supervised hands-free driving and fully driverless mobility fit into one technology journey, and why trust, earned through safety and consistent performance, is the real license to operate. A conversation about the most human of technologies being rebuilt around intelligence that adapts to us, and what customers a decade from now will consider ordinary that still feels extraordinary today.

sessions.title: Global Champions, European Roots
sessions.description: For all the talk of Europe falling behind, world-class companies are still being built here. This conversation is with two people who've done it. Nik Storonsky built Europe's most valuable private technology company in a decade, serving tens of millions of customers in more than forty markets. John Elkann has spent his career building and rebuilding European businesses with global reach. Together they ask what it takes to scale from here: how you build and keep exceptional teams, what happens to an established industry when someone arrives to do it differently and how AI is reshaping companies and the industries they operate in.

sessions.title: Beyond the pilot: how Juventus makes startup innovation compound
sessions.description: Most club innovation stalls at the pilot stage. Juventus built the Forward Squad to fix that: a three-tier programme (Player, Champion, Ally) designed so that each season's work builds on the last rather than starting from zero. The session covers live pilots across AI digital humans, voice-based fan emotion analysis and athlete performance technology, along with the handover between cohorts. For founders and investors, it's a practical look at what scaling innovation inside a major sports organisation actually requires.

sessions.title: The state of startups and VC in Italy
sessions.description: The Founder and CEO of Dealroom, the European intelligence platform on the startup world and investments, will open the session with an overview of the startup ecosystem in Italy. He will tell us how the ecosystem has performed this year and how it positions itself compared to other European ecosystems closer to us, such as Spain or France. He will discuss the growth trajectory, the challenges still to be faced, and the opportunities ahead. In short, he will provide all speakers and the audience with a precise picture of the boundaries within which this crucial sector operates.

sessions.title: Teaching Robots to Work: World Models and Adaptive Robotics for Manufacturing
sessions.description:
How can robots learn new tasks faster and improve beyond the data collected in the real world? This masterclass explores the full learning loop, from cold-start data collection and imitation learning to world models that scale training beyond physical demonstrations. Embodied AI will show how robotic policies are trained today from real-world data, while Saturn Dynamics will introduce how world models can generate large-scale interactive experience for policy training, evaluation and adaptation. We will discuss how a small initial dataset and policy can be expanded through simulated rollouts, enabling robots to explore many more task variations and improve performance on downstream tasks without proportionally increasing physical data collection
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Infinite Intelligence, Finite Planet: the hidden cost of growth in the age of AI
sessions.description:
AI feels limitless. The resources powering it are not.
Behind every prompt, model and data centre there is a physical world made of energy, water, land, materials and people. As AI accelerates the way we build, invest and grow, understanding its environmental, social and economic sustainability means looking beyond what technology can do and asking what it takes to make it possible.
This interactive masterclass is a journey through time and space to explore the limits and opportunities emerging from this tension and the connections between the choices we make today and the consequences they can generate elsewhere today and tomorrow.
Sustainability is not an add-on, nor the responsibility of a sustainability team, it's part of the equation and a design variable to consider from the very beginning.
The masterclass is an invitation to think systemically, question what we take for granted and design innovation more consciously, taking responsibility for our role within a much larger system of interconnected resources, people and opportunities.

⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Design, Brand & AI: making creativity accessible to everyone with Canva
sessions.description:
Unlock the full potential of visual communication and smart automation. Through real-world scenarios, this practical workshop demonstrates how Canva empowers anyone to turn complex data and ideas into stunning presentations, marketing materials, and collaborative projects.
Discover how embedding AI into your daily routine drastically cuts down manual tasks, speeds up content creation, and turns creative intuition into fast execution.
An interactive session to master next-generation workflows and make high-quality design effortless for your entire team.
⚠️ Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.
This masterclass is proudly powered by our Scaleup Partner Canva.

sessions.title: The Long Game
sessions.description: Long before venture capital arrives, someone has to build the ground an ecosystem grows from: the universities, the research, the patient institutions that back a place for decades rather than quarters. This conversation is with the president of one of Italy's oldest and most influential foundations, a Turin institution with centuries of history, now reinventing how it works around data, evidence, and long-term impact. An engineer and former university rector by background, with years spent bridging Italian and American science and technology, he brings a rare double perspective: the rigor of someone who knows the technology from the inside, and the patience of an institution that measures its returns in generations, not funding rounds. A conversation about the role of foundations and territory in building an innovation ecosystem, why the deepest roots of Italian tech are often the least visible, and what it takes to turn a place with history into a place with a future.

sessions.title: Winning Global Capital
sessions.description: Every Italian founder has heard the advice: to raise serious money, you have to leave. This conversation is proof you don't. It brings together a founder who built one of Italy's fastest-growing AI companies and the international investor who chose to lead its Series B, not despite where it was built, but because of what that team was building. The dominant playbook in their category came out of the US, aimed at English-speaking markets. They bet the opposite way, on data over hype and on the markets everyone else overlooked, and a global fund wrote one of its largest checks to back it. For the founders and future founders in the room, this is the practical version of the story that matters most: what actually makes a top-tier international investor say yes, what they look for before they wire the money.

sessions.title: Biology's Missing Data
sessions.description: Everyone talks about AI transforming biology, but the field has a problem no one likes to admit: the models can predict, they just can't experiment, and the high-quality data they need to learn from mostly doesn't exist yet. This keynote comes from an Italian founder building the missing layer between artificial intelligence and the lab, infrastructure that generates biological data at a scale, speed, and quality the field has never had, with the provenance and rigor that training a Bio x AI model actually demands. It's a look at why the bottleneck in AI for biology isn't compute but data, what changes when experiments run as software and results arrive in days instead of months, and why the companies that build this foundational layer may quietly become some of the most important in the industry.

sessions.title: From Personal Branding to Thought Leadership: how to build your presence on LinkedIn
sessions.description:
From debunking common myths and showcasing real creator journeys to uncovering lessons from the Top Voices program, Genio Media welcomes the LinkedIn News team to explore how to grow as a creator on LinkedIn. The goal: to equip you with practical tips and tools to build an authoritative professional presence through the knowledge you share.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Simplification is Innovation: how digital engineering enables speed and smart synchronisation in complex product development
sessions.description:
As vehicle complexity continues to grow, the ability to integrate, validate and optimize products faster than ever is becoming a critical competitive advantage. This masterclass explores how Digital Engineering is emerging as a new pillar of product integration, complementing the physical and functional integration approaches traditionally used by the automotive industry.

At the heart of this transformation is the concept of the Virtual Car: a digital environment where vehicles can be integrated, simulated, tested and refined before physical prototypes even exist, with the customer in the loop.

By leveraging high fidelity Physics Based and Data Driven models, Digital Integration and continuity, shared data and synchronized decision-making, Digital Engineering enables teams to better manage complexity while accelerating development speed and improving quality.

Through a combination of high-impact visuals, live demonstrations and real-world examples, the session will showcase how digital technologies are reshaping the way products are developed at Stellantis. Featuring Guglielmo Caviasso (STELLANTIS VP GLOBAL HEAD OF DIGITAL INTEGRATION AND VEHICLE VALIDATION) and Luca Miretti (STELLANTIS VEHICLE ENGINEERING AI PROGRAMS), the masterclass will demonstrate why simplification is no longer just an efficiency objective, but a powerful form of innovation that helps organizations move faster, collaborate smarter and deliver better products.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Inside the Machine: how LLMs actually work, and how to deploy them in legal practice
sessions.description:
Generative AI is now ubiquitous in legal work. What remains rare is a genuine understanding of what happens between the prompt and the output, and that is precisely where the difference lies between a mediocre result and one you can rely on professionally.
This workshop opens the black box: tokens, context windows, probabilistic generation, hallucinations. The mechanisms a lawyer needs to grasp in order to judge when a model can be trusted, when it cannot, and how to instruct it to produce defensible results.
Participants will leave with an operational framework for integrating LLMs into daily practice — from research to drafting with a clear understanding of where the tool ends and professional responsibility begins.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Vento: 200+ Bets on Italian Founders
sessions.description: This Wave event has become something of a tradition. Once again this year, a seasoned executive with decades of experience at Amazon and Apple opens with an update on Vento, where he chairs the Advisory Council: the progress and impact among early-stage Italian founders, now 200+ investments since 2022, at a pace of about 1.5 startups a week, alongside the venture building program, now in its sixth edition. This year he's joined on stage by two guests who represent the two sides of what Vento does. One is the founder of Cato, part of the investment portfolio and a story of conviction that compounds: backed once, backed again, and now growing fast. The other came up through Reef, Vento's venture building program, and this year's cohort, building a company from the ground up. Together, a live look at how early-stage Italian tech actually gets built, one bet and one founder at a time.

sessions.title: Algorithm vs Instinct
sessions.description: Two of the investors on this stage back founders the old-fashioned way, by meeting them, trusting an instinct built over years in the trenches, and betting on a person before the numbers make the case. The third barely uses instinct at all: his fund runs on an AI system that scans billions of data points to decide where the money goes, with the stated goal of nearly removing human judgment from the process. This is a real debate, not a panel. As AI reshapes how capital gets allocated, is the future of venture a better model, a sharper gut, or some uneasy marriage of the two? And what does it mean for the next founder walking into the room, hoping someone, or something, decides to believe in them?

sessions.title: Building the infrastructure for autonomous research
sessions.description:
Starting from a concrete scientific problem, participants will see how to structure a research graph, launch agent-driven experiments, inspect the resulting trajectory, and use the evidence collected to guide the next step. Autonomous science requires more than asking an AI model for answers. In this interactive masterclass, Paradigma will show how Flywheel turns a research objective into an executable loop of hypotheses, experiments, evidence, and next decisions. The session will offer a practical view of what autonomous research looks like today and how scientific teams can use models and infrastructure to accumulate progress over time.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Decoding Top Talent: a hands-on workshop on career preference data and AI-powered hiring
sessions.description:
Top talent doesn't move for the reasons most companies think. In this hands-on session, we'll share exclusive data on what drives career preferences among the world's top professionals, and show how AI is changing the way the best companies identify, engage, and hire them. Expect practical frameworks you can apply the same week.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Tech innovation needs public engagement: how to design STEM initiatives for social and business impact
sessions.description:
You are a main player in tech, utilities or digital innovation, but can you explain the value you bring to a classroom of students, a local community, or your next generation of talent? Tech companies often excel at future building, yet struggle to communicate it beyond expert circles. This workshop explores WHY engaging diverse publics through STEM education isn't a “nice to have,” but a strategic asset for startups and established tech organisations.
Investing in public STEM culture goes far beyond corporate social responsibility. It's a vital strategy to strengthen your talent pipeline, build trust, and anchor your company within the societal fabric that ultimately shapes the success of any technology.
Through concrete case studies and interactive exercises, you'll learn HOW it is possible to design meaningful outreach initiatives that enhance both social impact and business outcomes. You will leave with a new vision about the importance to inspire, educate, and connect with people.
⚠️Make sure you arrive at your booked Masterclass or Podcast no later than 5 minutes before the start - seats will be released to walk-ins after this time.

sessions.title: Seed to Scale
sessions.description: Every founder in this room is somewhere on the same climb, and this panel puts three different altitudes on one stage. One is at the very beginning: fresh capital, a small team, everything still to prove. One is in the thick of scaling, a product that works and customers who want more, now racing to grow without breaking what got them here. And one has already climbed higher, building one of Europe's most established companies in its category. Three Italian founders at three distinct stages of the journey, talking honestly about what actually changes as a company grows: what keeps you up at night at each phase, what you'd tell your earlier self, and why the hardest problem is never the one you expect. For anyone building or hoping to build, it's a rare chance to see the whole climb at once, from the people living each part of it right now.

sessions.title: Embodied Intelligence for Human Infrastructure: From Autonomous Vehicles to Autonomous Surgery
sessions.description: Surgery is the last $100B industry that still scales one pair of hands at a time. The history of surgery has progressively found less invasive ways to reach disease - from opening the body, to small incisions, to navigating the body through the vascular system itself. Mosaic Intelligence Labs builds the perception and robotics layer for incisionless surgery - the least invasive medicine we have, and also the hardest to scale. To decouple the quality and scale of output from the human labor input, the only remaining lever is to make each unit of human expertise go further. When we make the body's own highways navigable, endless possibilities open up for the future of interventional medicine, at scale.

speakers.name: Adam Jonas
speakers.bio: Adam Jonas is a Managing Director in Morgan Stanley's Equity Research department, serving as the Firm's Global Embodied AI/Robotics Strategist. Adam spent nearly three decades as an autos analyst, starting from when he joined the Firm in 1996, and is recognized globally as a thought leader in the automotive sector. His team has ranked No. 1 in each of the past three years (2023-2025) in the Extel (Institutional Investor) All-America Research Team survey for Autos & Auto Parts. In collaboration with his global research colleagues, Adam publishes insights on the future of AI-enabled robotics, autonomous vehicles, brain-computer interfaces, quantum, and the space economy. Adam is a Chartered Financial Analyst and earned his bachelor's degree in business administration (with distinction) from the University of Michigan. Adam frequently lectures on the future of mobility at Princeton University, Columbia University, and the University of Michigan. Adam currently serves on the Advisory Board of the Conrad Foundation and previously served on the Board of Directors of National Safe Place.

speakers.name: Aleksandr Konotopskyi
speakers.job_title: Founder and Chairman of the Supervisory Board
speakers.bio:
Aleksandr Konotopskyi is a serial entrepreneur. He was included in the list of 100 leaders who move the country forward by popular Ukrainian media Ukrainska Pravda and New Voice. Aleksandr was also recognized as Entrepreneur of the Year at the Security and Safety Entrepreneur Awards 2025 in the United Kingdom for his leadership in implementing and advancing innovations in the security sector. According to Forbes, he ranks 20th among Ukraine's richest people. Aleksandr was also recognized as the Entrepreneur of the Year in 2021 and has been featured in World of Forbes and the prestigious 30 Under 30 list. 

At the age of 21, Aleksandr launched an online store for security equipment. Within just four years, he propelled his company to the top of Ukraine’s distributors. However, Aleksandr's ambitions went even further. He aimed to create a product that could represent Ukraine on the global stage. This is how the Ajax smart security system was born. 

Ajax Systems is now Europe’s largest developer and manufacturer of security systems. The full-scale war and new challenges of 2022 didn’t stop the company’s growth. Ajax Systems successfully continued operations, relocating its production facilities to a safer region of Ukraine and resuming the production cycle in just five weeks. Additionally, new factories were launched in Turkey and Vietnam, while Ajax devices entered almost all markets in the world.

Currently, Ajax protects over 4,5 million end users and 330K PRO users in more than 180 countries worldwide. 

Ajax Systems consistently supports the development of engineering education in Ukraine, particularly through the Ajax Next initiative. In partnership with leading educational institutions, the company creates educational activities, establishes modern laboratories, and provides students with essential resources for practical training. Besides, the company supports cultural initiatives all over the world with the aim to preserve cultural heritage.

speakers.name: Alessandro Scortecci
speakers.bio:
Alessandro Scortecci is the Head of Direct Funds at CDP Venture Capital, reporting directly to the CEO. He manages 16 direct investment funds, leading a team of 100 professionals in the sourcing, analysis, and management of investment and divestment opportunities in startups and innovative SMEs — from tech transfer to late-stage growth. He also oversees value creation activities across a portfolio of over 400 companies.
Alessandro is a member of the Investment Committee for the Evolution Fund (2021) and was recently appointed to the Investment Committees of the Large Ventures Fund and the Startup Relaunch Fund. He also currently serves as interim Partner for the EnergyTech Fund.
Previously, Alessandro served as Head of Strategy, Business Development & Sustainability at the management company (SGR), where he built strong relationships with both Italian and international investors and partners. He led the development of the firm’s industrial plan, which introduced a sector-focused investment approach and an emphasis on portfolio value creation.
Since joining CDP Venture Capital in 2020, Alessandro has brought nearly 20 years of experience in venture capital and strategic consulting across the United States, United Kingdom, and the Middle East. Before that, he worked with major sovereign and institutional investors on investment strategy, portfolio management, innovation, and venture capital as a Partner at Boston Consulting Group.
Alessandro holds a cum laude degree in Civil Engineering from the University of Bologna, a Master’s in Engineering Management from Cornell University, and an MBA from INSEAD.

speakers.name: Alessandro Tommasi
speakers.bio: Public policy guy turned media entrepreneur. In love with the idea that change is possible. I founded Willmedia in 2020, Nos in 2023 and FutureProofSociety in 2024.

speakers.name: Alex Kendall
speakers.bio:
Alex Kendall co-founded Wayve in 2017 to reimagine autonomous mobility through embodied intelligence. Under his leadership, it’s one of the fastest-growing AI companies for autonomous driving.
A recognized world expert in AI and Robotics, Alex earned his Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge. Through his award-winning research in deep learning, he pioneered a new end-to-end AI approach to self-driving, building a general-purpose driving intelligence that can navigate the world without maps and make safe decisions in complex environments.
As CEO, Alex leads Wayve’s direction and execution, working closely with the leadership team, investors, and partners to scale and deploy its embodied AI software across millions of vehicles and robotaxi fleets worldwide. Alex was named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 Innovators list and was awarded an Order of the British Empire in 2025 for services to AI.

speakers.name: Alex Schmitt
speakers.bio: Alexander Schmitt is a Partner at Lightspeed, specialising in fintech, AI infrastructure, and application-layer technologies, including investments in companies like Paid, Helsing, and RobCo. Operating out of Europe, he is committed to empowering European startups to become global category leaders and strengthening the region’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. Previously, Alexander founded a fintech startup to address industry challenges he experienced directly. Before his current role, he was an investor at Cherry Ventures.

speakers.name: Alexandre Momeni
speakers.bio: Growing up as an Iranian immigrant made me aware early on that access to opportunity, security, and technology was not evenly distributed. I began my career at Goldman Sachs, drawn to the role capital plays in shaping global economies and societies, but quickly became convinced that entrepreneurs building at the frontier would be an even more powerful force for change. At General Catalyst, I partner with founders globally from the earliest stages through growth and beyond, with a focus on frontier intelligence, robotics, and science. I’m especially interested in moments when technological advances make entirely new products and businesses possible in critical industries. This includes working with founders pursuing difficult, consequential problems, such as Black Forest Labs, Chai Discovery, Mistral AI, Hippocratic AI, amongst others. Before joining GC, I spent a few years on the trading floor at Goldman Sachs, conducted AI research at Stanford, and built products at Nabla, learning to see the world through different questions and from different vantage points. Prior to that, I received a BS in Economics from the London School of Economics, an MS in Mathematics from École polytechnique, and an MS in Management from HEC Paris.

speakers.name: Anas Biad
speakers.bio: Anas Biad is a Partner at Sequoia. He focuses on the growth-stage (Series B+) across the U.S. and Europe and works with companies including Serval, Profound, Nominal, Avelios, Harvey, Pennylane, and Trade Republic. He joined Sequoia in 2021 from Silver Lake, where he was involved in several of the firm’s late-stage software investments. Prior to that, he was at Bain, advising on due diligence for tech companies in Asia and Europe. Anas grew up in Morocco and holds an MSc in Mathematics from École Polytechnique in France.

speakers.name: Andrea Bonabello
speakers.bio:
Exited founder turned investor, with a track record spanning startups, public markets and M&A.
Built a 30-startup portfolio, led an IPO and 4 acquisitions as CFO of a listed tech company, and now backs frontier technologies across Europe as GP at NVM Ventures, a Luxembourg-based multi-compartment venture capital fund designed to bring together leading emerging managers through dedicated strategies, starting with early-stage dual-use technologies.

speakers.name: Andrea Gennarini
