posizione di Amministratore Delegato presso aziende specializzate in Digital Health, advertising ed 
Healthtech. Nel 2016 entra nel consiglio di amministrazione di Talent Garden. Ha ricoperto la carica di 
Presidente Confindustria Giovani e Vice Presidente Confindustria Digitale. È stato membro del 
consiglio di amministrazione del Sole 24 Ore S.p.A. e dell’Università LUISS Guido Carli; lo è tutt’ora 
della società Online Sim e da giugno 2024 è membro del CDA del Politecnico di Torino. Da aprile 2024 
a luglio 2026 ha ricoperto il ruolo di Presidente Esecutivo di Zest S.p.A.

speakers.name: Marco Gilli
speakers.bio:
Marco Gilli is a Professor of Electrical Engineering at the Politecnico di Torino (Technical University of Torino). From February 2012 to March 2018, he served as Rector of the Politecnico di Torino. From 2012 to 2014, he served as President of CESAER (Conference of European Schools for Advanced Engineering Education and Research). From July 2019 to July 2024, he served as a Science and Technology Counselor at the Embassy of Italy in the USA. Since April 2024, he has been appointed President of the “Compagnia di San Paolo” Foundation.
His research focuses primarily on nonlinear circuits, systems, and neural networks, including machine learning and AI applications. He is the author or co-author of more than 200 scientific publications.  Since 2019 Marco Gilli has been consistently included in World's 2% Top Scientists ranking compiled by Stanford University in collaboration with Elsevier.
Marco Gilli has been a Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) since 2005. He has been responsible for many national and international research projects and partnership agreements with national and international companies, including manufacturing, energy, and IT industries.

speakers.name: Marco Molinaro
speakers.job_title: Cybersecurity Lead for Italy and Greece

speakers.name: Marco Pavone
speakers.bio:
Dr. Marco Pavone is an Associate Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics at Stanford University, where he directs the Autonomous Systems Laboratory. He also leads autonomous vehicle research at NVIDIA. Prior to joining Stanford, he was a Research Technologist in the Robotics Section at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory. He received his Ph.D. in Aeronautics and Astronautics from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2010.
His research centers on Physical AI—the development of AI systems grounded in physics, perception, and control that can operate robustly in the real world. His work spans applications including self-driving cars, autonomous aerospace vehicles, and general-purpose robotic systems. He has received numerous honors, including the Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers from President Barack Obama.

speakers.name: Marell Evans
speakers.bio:
Marell is the General Partner and Founder of Exceptional Capital. With over a decade of enterprise sales and investment experience, Marell leverages a range of professional expertise and a diverse network to support founders in the earliest stages of their journey. As an operator and investor across various sectors - including industrial automation, robotics, information technology, enterprise software, cybersecurity and fintech - Marell strives to empower the most innovative and exceptional founders.
Marell credits his experience as an athlete and Division 1 football player as having instilled a drive for excellence, enthusiasm, and a compassionate approach to collaboration and leadership. He believes that mentorship is fundamental for future leadership in tech and venture, and supports that through various initiatives, inclusive of Exceptional Capital’s internship program.
Marell is a Kauffman Fellow and graduated from the University of Michigan.

speakers.name: Marta Casassa
speakers.company: Opening Future, a joint project by Google Cloud, Intesa Sanpaolo, and TIM Enterprise

speakers.name: Martin Coulter
speakers.bio:
Martin Coulter is News Editor at Sifted, the Financial Times-backed publication covering European startups and venture capital. He oversees Sifted’s daily news coverage and reports on technology, AI and the companies shaping Europe’s startup ecosystem.
Before joining Sifted, Martin previously covered the technology sector for Reuters, the Financial Times and Business Insider.

speakers.name: Martìn Jerch
speakers.job_title: Head of Department, Entrepreneurship and Investors

speakers.name: Matan Grinberg
speakers.bio:
Matan Grinberg is CEO and Co-Founder of Factory, the global leader in self-improving software development with customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and more.
Matan studied string theory at Princeton and UC Berkeley, before co-founding Factory.

speakers.name: Matteo Luischi
speakers.job_title: Chief Management Officer & UK Interim Country Manager
speakers.bio:
Chief Management Officer & UK Interim Country Manager, Prima
Matteo Luischi is Chief Management Officer and UK Interim Country Manager at Prima, one of Europe’s leading insurtech companies.
As Chief Management Officer, Matteo has executive responsibility for Product and Engineering across Prima, alongside driving the prioritization and execution of the company’s key strategic initiatives across markets. He also leads Prima’s AI strategy, accelerating the adoption of AI across the organization and turning emerging technologies into scalable products, operational improvements, and measurable business impact.
Since joining Prima in 2017 as Head of Claims, Matteo has played a key role in the company’s growth and international expansion. He contributed to the launch of Prima’s operations in the UK and Spain and has since held several leadership positions, including Chief Strategy Officer and Chief of Staff.
Alongside his Group responsibilities, Matteo currently leads Prima’s UK business as Interim Country Manager.
Before joining Prima, Matteo worked at The Boston Consulting Group. He holds an MBA from Harvard Business School.

speakers.name: Matteo Villa
speakers.job_title: Head of STEM engagement and communication

speakers.name: Mattia Voltaggio
speakers.bio:
Mattia Voltaggio (Roma, 1982) è Head of Joule, la Scuola di Eni per l’Impresa, iniziativa attraverso cui Eni promuove l’innovazione, l’imprenditorialità e la crescita di startup ad alto potenziale.
Dopo la laurea in Conservazione dei Beni Culturali presso l’Università degli Studi di Roma “La Sapienza”, completa la propria formazione con un Master in Business Administration presso l’Università Commerciale “Luigi Bocconi”.
Nel 2006 entra in Eni, dove sviluppa un’esperienza pluriennale in ambito comunicazione istituzionale, corporate identity e brand management, contribuendo a progetti strategici di posizionamento e valorizzazione dell’immagine aziendale.
Nel 2016 entra a far parte della struttura del Chief Human Capital & Procurement Officer, supportando il management sui temi legati allo sviluppo del capitale umano, all’innovazione organizzativa e alla valorizzazione delle competenze. Questa esperienza consolida la sua visione dell’impresa come luogo di crescita delle persone e di sviluppo di nuove capacità imprenditoriali.
Dal 2020 guida Joule, la Scuola di Eni per l’Impresa, con l’obiettivo di promuovere la cultura imprenditoriale e sostenere la nascita e la crescita di startup innovative. Sotto la sua responsabilità vengono sviluppati programmi di incubazione, accelerazione e formazione rivolti a imprenditori, startup, studenti e innovatori. L’attività di Joule si estende anche a livello internazionale, attraverso progetti dedicati allo sviluppo dell’ecosistema imprenditoriale in Paesi africani come Congo, Costa d’Avorio e Kenya, contribuendo alla diffusione di competenze, opportunità e modelli di innovazione sostenibile.
Dal 2023 è inoltre Program Manager Officer di ROAD (Rome Advanced District), polo dedicato all’innovazione tecnologica e alla sostenibilità energetica promosso da Eni. Il progetto rappresenta un modello di collaborazione tra grandi imprese, startup, università e centri di ricerca, coinvolgendo partner quali Gruppo FS, Autostrade per l’Italia, Acea, Bridgestone, eFM, NextChem e Cisco. All’interno di ROAD coordina iniziative finalizzate ad accelerare lo sviluppo e l’adozione di tecnologie innovative in settori chiave per la transizione energetica e la competitività industriale.
Dal 2026 è anche Adjunct Professor di Etica e Responsabilità d’Impresa presso l’Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore, nell’ambito del Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Management Imprese e Mercati della Facoltà di Economia.

speakers.name: Max Junestrand
speakers.bio: Max Junestrand is the CEO and co-founder of Legora – the AI workspace for legal professionals – serving over 1000 customers across 50+ markets. Backed by leading investors including ICONIQ, General Catalyst, Benchmark, Redpoint Ventures, and Y Combinator, and supported by a world-class team of engineers and lawyers, Max is driving a new era of collaborative AI in the legal industry.

speakers.name: Merete Hverven
speakers.bio: Merete Hverven joined Visma as Chief Human Resources Officer in 2011 and was appointed Deputy CEO in 2018 before taking on the role of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) in March 2020. As CEO, Merete is responsible for planning and executing Visma’s long-term strategy, focusing on innovation, operational excellence and sustainable growth in existing markets as well as strategic expansion into new geographies.Merete is a strong advocate for building a high-performing, engaging and inclusive workplace. With her direct leadership style, ability to execute, and genuine focus on people, Merete is described as a driven, effective, and deeply committed leader by her colleagues. In 2024 she was recognized by Thinkers50 as one of the world’s most inspiring leaders.In addition to holding board positions in several Visma companies, she also serves as a board member of Kongsberg Gruppen. Before joining Visma in 2011, Merete had several leading positions at Ernst & Young (now EY).Merete holds master’s degrees in international leadership and finance from the University of St Gallen and NHH Norwegian School of Economics.

speakers.name: Mia Ceran
speakers.bio: Mia Ceran is an Italian journalist, tv host and podcaster. She has started her career as an intern for CNN then moved to the main Italian newscasts as a reporter. She hosts the show TvTalk on Italian state television (a weekly summary of the main news and events), her videopodcast NowWhat? has brought together a community of informed and opinionarted individuals which has been growing rapidly and has reached a combined size of almost 1 million listeners/viewers across all platforms.

speakers.name: Michele Catasta
speakers.bio:
Michele Catasta is President & Head of AI at Replit, where he is shaping the future of software creation through AI agents. In 2024, he architected and led the launch of Replit Agent, which has driven over two orders of magnitude in company revenue growth to date. Previously, he was Head of Applied Research at Google X and Google Labs, focusing on Large Language Models and contributing to the coding capabilities of PaLM and PaLM 2.
Earlier in his career, Michele was a Research Scientist and Instructor at Stanford University, pioneering the application of Transformer architectures to source code. He earned a Ph.D. in Computer Science from EPFL and held research positions at MIT Media Lab, Google, and Yahoo Labs.
‍Beyond his operating roles, Michele is an active angel investor with more than 100 investments in the AI space, and serves (or has served) as an advisor to Bessemer, Coatue, Decibel, Fellows Fund, and Obvious.

speakers.name: Michele Pierri
speakers.job_title: Head of Creator Management & Editorial Team Italy

speakers.name: Mike Winkelmann
speakers.bio:
Beeple is a digital artist and graphic designer widely recognized as a pioneer in the realm of digital art and NFTs. Beeple gained international acclaim for his Everydays project, where he has created a new digital artwork every day for over 19 years, amassing a collection of thousands of pieces that reflect his creative evolution and contemporary cultural commentary.
Beeple’s work challenges traditional art paradigms, exploring the intersection of technology, art, and culture. His art often uses cutting-edge tools such as 3D rendering software and AI, pushing the boundaries of what digital media can achieve in storytelling and visual impact.
Institutional presentations include- the Deji Art Museum in China, Gibbes Museum of Art in South Carolina, M+ in Hong Kong, Crystal Bridges in Arkansas, LACMA in Los Angeles. And currently, MoCA in Wisconsin, where you can see Diffuse Control, a kinetic video sculpture that plays a continuously evolving video powered by custom AI models and real-time user interaction.

speakers.name: Morgan Samet
speakers.bio:
Morgan Samet is Managing Partner & Co-Head of the Lingotto Innovation Strategy, a $1.5 billion+ multi-stage growth strategy that invests in private and public companies at the forefront of exponential technology and business model innovation. She has 20 years of private and public markets experience across all sectors, geographies, and stages. Since Lingotto Innovation’s founding, she’s been instrumental in driving its strategy and investments, including major private deals in Databricks, Tempus AI (NASDAQ- TEM), Pony AI (NASDAQ- PONY), Enveda Biosciences, Trade Republic, Airwallex, RobCo, Kavak, Multiply Labs, and the BotCo.
Lingotto Innovation is focused on identifying extreme winners and supports visionary management teams in building the next generation of $100 billion+ companies by providing patient, long-term capital and unique access. The firm is deeply research-driven and invests thematically across AI & Technology, the Physical Economy, and Healthcare. In her role, Morgan leads an interdisciplinary team with decades of experience spanning investing, industry, and academia. She has been featured in Barron’s, Business Insider, and The Financial Times and has been a major speaker at many top tech conferences and universities including Harvard, MIT, Penn State. She sits on the advisory board for Vento Ventures, a European early-stage fund and venture builder, and helps host Italian Tech Week (now the Wave Conference), which is one of the biggest technology conferences in Europe with over 15,000 attendees.
Before Lingotto, Morgan was a partner at a long-term crossover fund, Belfer Management, a public markets investor at Pzena, and a private investor at THL Partners. She started her career at Goldman Sachs advising fin-tech companies, banks, and asset managers during the financial crisis. Morgan earned her MBA from Harvard Business School, where she was awarded a Rock and Lebow fellowship for entrepreneurship and briefly led e-commerce for a rapidly growing fashion start-up. She graduated from the Schreyer Honors College at the Pennsylvania State University, where she helped launch and ran a multi-million public equities fund that still exists today. She now serves on the Finance Advisory Board for the Smeal College of Business at Penn State.
Lingotto Investment Management is an ~$11bn AUM alternative investment management company. Founded in 2023, Lingotto is backed with founding capital from Exor N.V. in addition to top institutional investors. Exor N.V. is one of Europe’s largest diversified holding companies.

speakers.name: Nazanin Daneshvar
speakers.bio:
Here's a polished conference bio for Nazanin-
Nazanin Daneshvar is a venture capital investor and General Partner at AngelInvest, one of Europe's most active early-stage investment platforms, where she deploys capital from a €160 million fund focused on AI, enterprise software, and technology startups across Europe and the United States.
With over two decades of experience spanning software engineering, entrepreneurship, and venture investing, Nazanin brings a rare combination of deep technical expertise and operational leadership to the investment world. She previously served as Entrepreneur in Residence and Acting Partner at EQT Ventures, where she specialized in AI-first investments across infrastructure and application layers.
She is the founder of Takhfifan, Iran's first and leading discount and cashback platform, which she built to over 15 million users, 200,000 partners, and 350 employees before filing for IPO — making it the most successful female-founded startup in the country's history.
Nazanin has been recognized by the United Nations as one of five women worldwide selected as a UN Advocate for Entrepreneurship under UNCTAD's eTrade for Women program. Her work has been featured in the Financial Times, Forbes, The Guardian, Washington Post, TechCrunch, and Der Spiegel, among others.
A passionate advocate for female leadership in tech and entrepreneurship, she is a sought-after speaker, mentor, and board advisor across the global startup ecosystem.

speakers.name: Nik Storonsky
speakers.bio:
Nik Storonsky is the Founder and CEO of Revolut, Europe’s most valuable private technology company and one of the world’s leading fintech platforms, serving over 75 million customers globally.
Nik is also the founder of QuantumLight, the world's first fully systematic, AI-driven venture capital firm. Powered by its proprietary AI/ML model “Aleph,” QuantumLight is designed to select and invest in outlier tech companies at scale and systematically outperform top-decile VC returns.
Before founding Revolut, Nik was an Emerging Markets Equity Derivatives Trader at Credit Suisse and Lehman Brothers, managing a $2B+ portfolio across derivatives and FX. He holds an M.S. in Applied Physics and Mathematics and an M.A. in Economics. Outside of the office, Nik is an adventurer, known as a championship swimmer, mountaineer, and keen kite surfer.

speakers.name: Paddy Dillon
speakers.bio: Paddy is a Principal at Left Lane and co-leads its European office in London. Left Lane is a global venture capital firm with over $3BN AUM that was founded in New York in 2019. Paddy leads Series A-C rounds, focusing on founders building in categories such as consumer internet, AI, fintech, and more. He serves on the boards of Lexroom and Buena, and as a board observer at HOLY, Kittl and Kings League, amongst others.

speakers.name: Paolo Cerioli
speakers.job_title: Chief Innovation and Information Technology Officer
speakers.bio:
Paolo Cerioli serves as Fincantieri Chief Innovation and Information Technology Officer.
Prior to joining Fincantieri, Paolo was Eni Group Head of Open Innovation & Ecosystems Development, responsible for leading innovation processes, developing innovation ecosystem and shaping partnerships; fueling the short-long term technology innovation projects and agenda for Eni’s businesses and functions.
Prior to joining Eni, Paolo was Industry Leader Oil & Gas Advisory Services for Mediterranean Area in EY, and furthermore spent more than 10 years in The Boston Consulting Group (BCG) with main focus on Energy and Industrial Goods sectors in Italy, Europe and Middle East.
Paolo graduated with a Master in Mechanical Engineering and he holds an MBA.

speakers.name: Paolo Fois
speakers.bio: Paolo Fois is the co-founder and CEO of Lexroom. Paolo founded Lexroom in 2023, setting out to fix a legal profession still buried in manual work. Where general-purpose LLMs tend to hallucinate, he built Lexroom around a proprietary legal database that grounds every answer in verified legal sources. Today more than 15% of legal proceedings in Italy run through Lexroom. The company is ranked 2nd among the fastest-growing startups in Southern Europe and has raised more than $73M. When Paolo is not working, he enjoys open-water sports, reading and cooking.

speakers.name: Paolo Pio
speakers.bio: Paolo Pio is Co-Founder and General Partner at Exceptional Ventures, a London-based early-stage VC firm helping people live longer, healthier, and happier lives - maximising Joyspan®. Formerly MD Europe at Joyance Partners and an exec at Cisco, he has backed 70+ startups and is on a mission to drive the global health and wellness revolution.

speakers.name: Patrizia Celia
speakers.job_title: Head of Large Caps & Investment Vehicles, Equity Primary Markets

speakers.name: Petar Veličković
speakers.bio:
Petar Veličković is a Senior Staff Research Scientist at Google DeepMind, Affiliated Lecturer at the University of Cambridge, and an Associate of Clare Hall, Cambridge. He holds a PhD in Computer Science from the University of Cambridge (Trinity College), obtained under the supervision of Pietro Liò. Petar’s research concerns aligning neural networks to (classical) computation, to assess and improve their out-of-distribution generalisation ability. Particularly, Petar focusses on neural algorithmic reasoning (featured in VentureBeat), graph representation learning and categorical and geometric deep learning (a topic he has co-written a proto-book about). For Petar’s contributions, he is recognised as an ELLIS Scholar in the Geometric Deep Learning Program. Petar is the first author of Graph Attention Networks—a popular convolutional layer for graphs—and Deep Graph Infomax—a popular self-supervised learning pipeline for graphs (featured in ZDNet). His research has been used in substantially improving travel-time predictions in Google Maps (featured in Endgadget, VentureBeat, CNET, The Verge and ZDNet), guiding intuition of mathematicians towards new top-tier theorems and conjectures (featured in Nature, Science, Quanta Magazine, New Scientist,
The Independent, Sky News, The Sunday Times, la Repubblica and The
Conversation), the first full AI system for tactical suggestions in association
football (featured in Financial Times, The Athletic, The Economist, New Scientist, Wired, MIT Technology Review, The Verge and El País), and the first AI-assisted top-percentile result in competitive programming.

speakers.name: Philipp Herzig
speakers.bio: Philipp Herzig is Chief Technology Officer of SAP SE. In this role, Herzig leads SAP’s technology strategy, research, innovation, corporate development, technology ecosystem, startup engagement, and incubation including Business AI and Sustainability. In addition to AI and sustainability as major incubation topics, the Chief Technology Office also focuses on topics such as quantum computing.

speakers.name: Pier Luigi Pisa
speakers.bio: Journalist and writer, he is the author of Valeva la pena tentare – Sam Altman, OpenAI e il sogno di un’intelligenza artificiale per tutti (“It Was Worth Trying – Sam Altman, OpenAI and the Dream of Artificial Intelligence for Everyone”), published by Apogeo in October 2025, as well as the thematic series Capire l’Intelligenza Artificiale (“Understanding Artificial Intelligence”) and L’intelligenza artificiale e lo studio (“Artificial Intelligence and Learning”), both published by GEDI. He has written numerous series produced for Repubblica TV about some of the visionary minds of our time, including Essere Elon Musk (“Being Elon Musk”), Chi è Pavel Durov? – Il fondatore di Telegram (“Who Is Pavel Durov? – The Founder of Telegram”) and Scatti al futuro (“Snapshots of the Future”). For One Podcast, he wrote and produced the innovation series Non sapevo che – storie intelligenti che vale la pena ascoltare (“I Didn’t Know That – Smart Stories Worth Listening To”).

speakers.name: Pietro Bezza
speakers.bio: Founder turned VC. Led Seed in Aikido Security, Dust, Plain, TrueLayer, Typeform and + 25 tech companies built by few and loved by many.

speakers.name: Rafal Modrzewski
speakers.bio:
Rafal Modrzewski is the CEO and co- founder of ICEYE, which owns and operates the world’s
largest constellation of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites. The company delivers near
real- time Earth observation capabilities that support critical decision - making in national
security, defence, and disaster response. ICEYE was the first to successfully miniaturize a SAR
satellite making it possible to launch more units, more frequently, and achieve rapid revisit of
any location on Earth, day or night, in all w eather conditions.
Since co- founding the project with Pekka Laurila in 2012 and formally launching ICEYE in 2014.
Modrzewski has led the company’s growth from a student initiative into a global space and
defence technology leader. He has been at the forefront of ICEYE’s tech nical innovation and
strategic direction, overseeing its expansion into new markets and mission domains. His
engineering leadership played a central role in the company’s world - first SAR developments,
which earned him recognition on the Forbes 30 Under 30 Technology list in 2018.
Modrzewski is also one of the most recognized voices shaping the future of space - based
capabilities for defence and security and a frequent speaker at defence, technology, and policy
forums.
Before ICEYE, Modrzewski worked at VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, focusing on
RFID and wireless sensing technologies. He studied Electrical Engineering at Warsaw University
of Technology, and completed his graduate work in Radio Science and Engi neering at Aalto
University. At Aalto, he led the on - board data handling team for Aalto - 1, Finland’s first
nanosatellite

speakers.name: Riccardo Bassetto
speakers.bio:
Riccardo joined Will Media in 2021 and launched the podcast division. After the merger with Chora Media, he became Head of Operations of the new organization, driving the company's growth by working on people, processes and technology.
Alongside Riccardo Haupt, he co-hosts Actually podcast. He also writes a weekly newsletter, Technicismi, covering trends at the intersection of business, media and technology.

speakers.name: Roberta Marracino
speakers.job_title: Talent Lead, Accenture Italy and Greece
speakers.bio:
Roberta Marracino is Head of Talent for Accenture Italy and Greece. In her role, she is supporting organizations in the transformation of work, workforce, skills, and organizational models.
Roberta Marracino is part of the Accenture Italy leadership team and reports to the CEO, Teodoro Lio.
At Accenture since 2022, Roberta previously led the Strategy Consulting team and contributed to the definition and implementation of strategic plans and initiatives, including in the ESG space, within the financial services sector.
Roberta has extensive experience in the field of strategic consulting, in financial institutions, and in transformation programs.
Before joining Accenture, she served as Head of ESG Strategy and Impact Banking at UniCredit Group, where she led the development of the ESG and Social Impact Banking strategy and its implementation across all Group geographies and functions.
Previously, she served as a Board Member of BPER Group and was a member of the Risk and Control Committee and the Remuneration and Nomination Committees. Roberta has also been a Corporate Executive at Zurich Insurance and SACE, and has extensive experience from McKinsey & Company.
Throughout her career, Roberta has championed and founded several non-profit initiatives including Associazione Valore D, focused on women’s empowerment, and Studio Ergo Lavoro and Push to Open, both dedicated to the new generations.
Roberta is also a Board Member of the Fondazione Italiana Accenture, which works in the areas of social integration and youth employment inclusion, and of the Accademia Teatro alla Scala, which nurtures talents and the crafts of the performing arts.
Born in Udine, she graduated in Economics at University of Trieste and holds an MBA in International Business from MIB School of Management. Roberta lives and works in Milan.  

A passionate lover of mathematics and contemporary art, her favourite book is “Fermat’s Last Theorem” — a true story of passion and dedication, mistakes and perseverance.

speakers.name: Roma van der Walt
speakers.bio: Roma van der Walt, MSc, is a thought leader in the emerging field of female physiology and performance optimization through data, and is pioneering a systems-based approach to women’s health and performance. She is the founder and CEO of Vitelle, a health intelligence company building the first scalable, expert-augmented decision layer for female high-performance sport.

speakers.name: Rosemary Leith
speakers.company: Bolon Capital / Harvard Berkman Klein Centre
speakers.bio: As an investor Rosemary is deeply experienced in early stage deep tech from start-up, through scale up  to sale and from listing to FTSE 100. She is a governance leader both on tech policy and as a member of the board as well as senior advisor to CEO's including ProtonAG, ICG plc, Universal Quantum, SandboxAQ (an AI and Quantum company spun out of Google) and EIT - The Ellison Institute of Technology. She recently joined the Foundation Board of IMD, one of Europe’s leading business schools. She is a fellow at Harvard’s Berkman Klein Centre and was a Co-Founder of the World Wide Web Foundation, committed to gender equality online and responsible AI. She has been a Chair of Risk, Remuneration Committees and Senior Independent Director with a focus on technology and innovation strategy, deeptech and fintech. Committed to the arts she serves on the board of BAFTA and the Royal Academy and previously the National Gallery, London where she Chaired the Digital Advisory board.

speakers.name: Roxanne Varza
speakers.bio: Roxanne is currently the Director of STATION F, the world's biggest startup campus based in Paris, France. She is also an angel and scout investor, and sits on the board of media company NRJ Group. Prior to STATION F, she was the Editor of TechCrunch France and the Startup Lead for Micorosft in France. She also cofounded Tech.eu (now Webrazzi), StartHer (now part of SISTA) and the Failcon Paris conference.

speakers.name: Sachin Sachin
speakers.bio: Sachin is a robotics researcher in the Bio-Inspired Soft Robotics Group at the Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia in Genova, Italy. Working with Prof. Barbara Mazzolai, he leads research on subterranean locomotion and agricultural robotics, developing plant-root-inspired robotic systems for subsoil monitoring, intervention, and navigation. Drawing inspiration from roots and organisms such as earthworms, he explores efficient ways for robots to move through complex underground environments. Sustainability is central to his approach, with an emphasis on integrating soil health considerations into both robot design and operation. Alongside his subterranean robotics research, Sachin develops soft hybrid grippers for harvesting agricultural produce. He brings a strong foundation in soft robotics, having completed his doctoral research on soft grippers for food handling at Ritsumeikan University, Japan. He holds an M.Tech in Mechanical Engineering from NIT Jalandhar and spent a semester pursuing doctoral studies at IIT Bombay before moving to Japan. Previously, he worked as a design engineer in the R&D team of LMW’s machine tool division. Before moving into robotics research, he also helped maintain his family farm, gaining practical knowledge of agricultural machinery and farming processes. His experience across industry, research, and hands-on farming brings a grounded perspective to the development of robotics for soil and agriculture.

speakers.name: Sebastian Mallaby
speakers.job_title: Paul A. Volcker Senior Fellow for International Economics
speakers.bio: Sebastian Mallaby is the Paul A. Volcker senior fellow for international economics at the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR). A two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist, he is the author of six books, including More Money Than God- Hedge Funds and the Making of a New Elite and The Power Law- Venture Capital and the Making of the New Future, which have become investment classics. His latest book is The Infinity Machine- Demis Hassabis, DeepMind, and the Quest for Superintelligence. An experienced journalist and public speaker, Mallaby’s interests cover a wide variety of domestic and international issues, including the technology sector, central banks, financial markets, the implications of the rise of newly emerging powers, and the intersection of economics and international relations. His study of American economic statecraft, The Man Who Knew- The Life & Times of Alan Greenspan, won the 2016 Financial Times/McKinsey Business Book of the Year Award and the 2017 George S. Eccles Prize in Economic Writing. His earlier works are The World’s Banker, a portrait of the World Bank under James Wolfensohn that was named as an “Editor’s Choice” by the New York Times; and After Apartheid, which was named by the New York Times as a “Notable Book.” An essay in the Financial Times said of The World’s Banker, “Mallaby’s book may well be the most hilarious depiction of a big organization and its controversial boss since Michael Lewis’s Liar’s Poker.” Before joining CFR, Mallaby served eight years as a columnist and editorial board member at the Washington Post and spent thirteen years with the Economist. While at the Economist, he worked in London, where he wrote about foreign policy and international finance; in Africa, where he covered Nelson Mandela’s release and the collapse of apartheid; and in Japan, where he covered the breakdown of the country’s political and economic consensus. Between 1997 and 1999, Mallaby was the Economist’s Washington bureau chief and wrote the magazine’s weekly Lexington column on American politics and foreign policy. In 2015, he helped to found a startup, InFacts.org, a web publication making the fact-based case for Britain to remain in the European Union. Mallaby was educated at Oxford, graduating in 1986 with a first class degree in modern history. After eighteen years in Washington, DC, he moved to London in 2014, where he lives with his wife, Zanny Minton Beddoes, editor in chief of the Economist.

speakers.name: Sir Tim Berners-Lee
speakers.bio:
Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN in Switzerland. Since then, he founded the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), The Open Data Institute, the World Wide Web Foundation, and developed the Solid Protocol. As CTO and Co-Founder of Inrupt, he has been a tireless advocate for shared standards, open web access for all and the power of individuals on the web.

A firm believer in the positive power of technology, Sir Tim was named in Time magazine’s list of the most important people of the 20th century. He is an Emeritus Professor of Computer Science at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and University of Oxford and has been the recipient of several honorary degrees and awards, including the Seoul Peace Prize and the Turing Prize widely recognised as akin to the Nobel Prize for Computing. He was knighted in 2004 and later appointed to the Order of Merit by Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II.

speakers.name: Sonali De Rycker
speakers.bio:
Sonali joined the Accel team in London in 2008 and has witnessed the European ecosystem come of age firsthand. She focuses on AI, consumer (especially marketplace), next generation financial services and software companies.
Sonali was responsible for Accel’s investments in Spotify, which went public in 2018, Letgo, which joined forces with OfferUP in 2020, and Avito, which was acquired in 2015 by Naspers. In addition, Sonali led Accel's investments in Calastone, which was acquired by The Carlyle Group in October 2020, and Wallapop, which was acquired by Naver earlier this year.
Sonali’s current portfolio includes Kry, Monzo, Perceptic, Primer, Omnea, sennder, Shift Technology and Soldo.
Prior to Accel, Sonali was a partner at Atlas Venture. She attended Bryn Mawr College in Pennsylvania, holds an MBA from Harvard Business School and grew up in Mumbai, India.

speakers.name: Sophie Evans
speakers.bio: Sophie is Global Creative Strategy Director at Teads Studio and an expert in creative optimisation. With nearly two decades of experience spanning adtech, broadcast media, and creative partnerships, Sophie helps brands navigate creative decisions and the convergence of CTV and digital advertising. By championing marketing science, she provides actionable best practices to push creative boundaries while driving measurable brand growth.

speakers.name: Stefania Ruggeri
speakers.job_title: Direttrice Centro di Ricerca CREA Alimenti e Nutrizione, Roma
speakers.company: CREA- Consiglio per la Ricerca in Agricoltura e l’Analisi dell’Economia Agraria
speakers.bio:
Stefania Ruggeri è Direttrice del Centro di Ricerca CREA Alimenti e Nutrizione. Ricercatrice Nutrizionista e professoressa incaricata di “Food Design per la Circular Economy” alla Facoltà di Medicina, dell’Università La Sapienza di Roma.  Dottorato di  Ricerca in Biotecnologie Alimentari e Master in Comunicazione della Scienza  e Giornalismo scientifico, ha  iniziato le sue ricerche conducendo studi sulla qualità alimentare per poi occuparsi, dopo una periodo di studi in Inghilterra, di alimentazione e salute in epoca precocenzionale e gravidanza. Affascinata dalle lettura dei testi di Bruno Munari, si appassiona poi  al  Design e  Food Design, idea e fonda  nel  2024 la Piattaforma di Ricerca CREA Italian Food Design, che applica il Design Thinking e il System Thinking per la progettazione e la realizzazione di progetti di ricerca sul cibo, sana alimentazione e nuovi sistemi alimentari.
È stata coordinatrice di progetti di ricerca finanziati dal Ministero della Salute e di progetti strategici per il CREA  e attualmente coordina un progetto finanziato dall’Agenzia Spaziale Italiana per lo sviluppo di un nuovo alimento (space food) ad alto potenziale nutrizionale e salutistico per le missioni spaziali a lunga durata. Ha al suo attivo numerose pubblicazioni scientifiche sulle tematiche- alimentazione e salute, qualità degli alimenti, Dieta Mediterranea e Food Design.  Attualmente accanto alla linea di ricerca sui nuovi alimenti per lo Spazio, coordina il progetto CREA- “Enciclopedia della Cucina Italiana” e sta creando una rete internazionale dedicata allo sviluppo della Gastronomia Computazionale, una disciplina emergente che integra scienza degli alimenti, patrimonio gastronomico e Intelligenza Artificiale.
Ha partecipato alla redazione di documenti istituzionali e di documenti di policy italiani ed internazionali tra cui “Le Linee Guida per una Sana Alimentazione Italiana”, coordinando gruppi di esperti nazionali e ha rappresentato l’ex-INRAN e il CREA in workshop istituzionali e in eventi di rilevanza strategica a Bruxelles, in Oman e in Cina e in tavoli di lavoro nazionali ed internazionali.
Per la professionalità nel settore della Chimica e Tecnologie Alimentari, della Scienza della Nutrizione e del Food Design e per le capacità comunicative ha avuto il conferimento di incarichi di docenza da importanti università italiane, con l’affidamento di corsi di Laurea Magistrale e in corsi Master di I e II livello. Ha svolto attività seminariale nell'ambito di corsi di laurea, dottorati di ricerca e corsi di specializzazione e perfezionamento presso numerosi atenei nazionali e nell’ambito di percorsi formativi internazionali.
Voce autorevole nel campo della nutrizione è invitata a trasmissioni televisive e intervistata da testate nazionali e internazionali. Ha pubblicato- “La Nuova Dieta Mediterranea” (Gribaudo, edizioni 2014 e 2015) e “Mamma che fame. Adolescenti e cibo- i consigli e le ricette della nutrizionista” (ed. Sonzogno), 2018. Il suo ultimo libro è “Cibi Falsi” pubblicato nel 2025 da Newton Compton scritto con Riccardo Fargione.
Futuro, immaginazione le sue parole preferite.

speakers.name: Stefano Neri
speakers.job_title: Responsabile Ingegneria, Tecnologie Rotabili e Innovazione
speakers.bio: Stefano Neri is Head of Engineering, Rolling Stock Technologies and Innovation at Trenitalia (FS Group)

speakers.name: Susan Phan
speakers.bio:
Susan Phan is the CFO of Pigment, a business planning and performance management platform that combines dynamic modeling, AI agents, and an intuitive UX to help teams make intelligent decisions with speed and clarity.  Across finance, sales, supply chain, and other business functions, companies like Unilever, Snowflake, and Anthropic use Pigment to plan ahead and act with confidence.

Before Pigment, Susan was CFO & COO of Gem, a recruiting software company backed by Accel, Greylock, and ICONIQ.  Previously she led Strategic Finance at Dropbox, where she played a key role in taking the company public in 2018.  Susan started her career in investment banking at Centerview Partners, where she advised on over $6 billion of transactions.

speakers.name: Teodoro Lio
speakers.bio:
Teodoro Lio, starting September 1st 2024, is the CEO of Accenture Italy and a member of Accenture's Global Executive Leadership Team as Market Unit Lead of the ITG Region, which includes Italy and Greece.
Since joining Accenture in 2001, Lio has worked closely with key players in the national and international industry landscape, focusing on value creation through technology and digital transformation, with a strong focus on innovation and enhancing the spirit of entrepreneurship.
Prior to taking on the role of CEO, he was Accenture Lead for Products which include key sectors of Italy’s economy, from consumer goods to retail, from infrastructure and transportation to pharmaceutical and from automotive to heavy industry. He was the Head of a geographic region that comprises Italy, Central Europe and Greece. In parallel, he maintained his role as Europe Lead for Automotive & Mobility which he has held since 2018.
During his career, he has launched and led complex transformation programs in the areas of connected products, product-to-service transformations and digital customer interaction working with leading global technology partners.
Lio built his impressive international experience during his overseas assignments in China and ASEAN (Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand) and by holding roles of increasing responsibility in Europe, USA, and Brazil. His broad and deep perspective on the multicultural challenges that global players face is much valued by clients and is enhanced by his commitment to Accenture’s drive for Diversity & Inclusion and Gender Equality.
He holds a Bachelor Degree in Economics from the University of Turin.
Teodoro Lio is 52 years old. He is married, he has two children and he lives in Turin, Italy.

speakers.name: Tom Conca
speakers.bio:
Tommaso Conca is a Partner at QuantumLight, where he leads the firm’s investment team. QuantumLight is the venture capital firm launched by Revolut founder Nik Storonsky, with over $700M in AUM. The firm takes a systematic, data-driven approach to venture, using its proprietary machine-learning model to identify and back exceptional founders, primarily at Series B and C across AI, cybersecurity, fintech and other technology categories. QuantumLight’s investments include ElevenLabs, Lovable, Aikido and Fireworks.
Before joining QuantumLight, Tom was an early employee at SellerX and, prior to that, worked on M&A transactions at UBS. He grew up in Italy and graduated cum laude from Bocconi University. Tom splits his time between London, Milan and San Francisco, although these days he probably spends more time flying between them than actually being in any of them.

speakers.name: Tom Wehmeier
speakers.bio: TBC

speakers.name: Tommaso Ghidini
speakers.bio:
Tommaso Ghidini is a senior executive at the European Space Agency (ESA), where he leads the Agency's Mechanical Engineering and Quality and Safety Departments, with corporate responsibilities across all ESA's missions.
His departments provide engineering expertise, technical authority and independent mission assurance across ESA's programmes, from advanced technology development to spacecraft and launch vehicle qualification and flight. He is also the architect of ESA's Technology Vision 2040, defining long-term priorities in areas including artificial intelligence and robotics, advanced manufacturing, propulsion, quantum technologies and next-generation flight systems.
Ghidini has spent his career at the intersection of advanced technology, industrial transformation and high-performance engineering. Before ESA, he worked at Airbus on the A380, A350 and A400M programmes and at the German Aerospace Centre (DLR). At ESA, he founded the Agency's Advanced Manufacturing initiative, accelerating the industrialisation of advanced technologies across Europe's space sector, strengthening critical supply chains and industrial resilience, and supporting the reshoring of strategic manufacturing capabilities in Europe.
He serves on the Board of Directors of Ferrari N.V., bringing his experience in technology, engineering and innovation across the space, automotive and high-performance industrial sectors. He is also an Adjunct Professor at Politecnico di Milano and a Lieutenant Colonel in the Italian Air Force Selected Reserve, Aeronautical Engineering Corps, where he contributes to its strategic positioning in the space domain and to the development of sovereign defence capabilities.
Ghidini holds a Ph.D. in Engineering Mechanics and is the bestselling author of Homo Caelestis, exploring the future of humanity beyond Earth.

speakers.name: Tommaso Masi
speakers.bio: Tommaso Masi, known online as TommyVerse, is a corporate finance professional specialized in structured finance and private credit. He shares analyses of global trends, corporate data, and economics through his channels on Instagram, YouTube and TikTok. He is also the co-host of the Better podcast and the author of the geopolitical book L'altra faccia del mondo, published by Sperling & Kupfer.

speakers.name: Tony Xu
speakers.bio:
Tony Xu is the CEO and co-founder of DoorDash (NASDAQ- DASH), one of the world's leading local commerce platforms that helps businesses of all kinds grow and innovate, connects consumers to the best of their neighborhoods, and gives people fast, flexible ways to earn. Since its founding in 2013, DoorDash has expanded to more than 40 countries, using technology and logistics to shape the future of local commerce and broaden access to opportunity.
Born in China, Tony came to America with his parents and grew up working in a restaurant alongside his mom. He and his co-founders started DoorDash to help local businesses succeed. Prior to co-founding DoorDash in 2013, Tony worked in Product at Square, led special projects for the CEO and CFO at eBay, and began his career at McKinsey and Company. Since January 2022, Tony has served on the board of directors of Meta Platforms, Inc., a technology company. He holds a B.S. with high honors in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research from UC Berkeley and an MBA from Stanford Graduate School of Business, where he was an Arjay Miller Scholar.

speakers.name: Verena Papik
speakers.bio: Verena Papik is Founder and CEO of Talkalytics, the emotion analytics layer for voice, used by FIFA, Meta, TED, Broadway and Copa Airlines to hear how fans and customers feel. She previously ran GTM for musical.ly ahead of its Billion-Dollar ByteDance acquisition and is a two-time Forbes 30 Under 30.

speakers.name: Victoria Botella
speakers.bio:
Victoria leads enterprise growth for OpenAI across Italy and Spain, partnering with large organizations to deploy AI solutions that drive transformation, productivity, and innovation. She brings over 12 years of experience building go-to-market strategies at Salesforce and Writer, helping businesses embrace emerging technologies and turn their potential into measurable impact.
Victoria holds a postgraduate degree in Philosophy from the University of Cambridge. This distinctive background shapes how she approaches AI- always asking not only what technology can do, but how it can meaningfully benefit businesses, individuals, and society. She is passionate about advancing OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

speakers.name: Virgílio Bento
speakers.bio:
V is the founder and CEO of Sword, the AI company for health. Sword operates as both a frontier AI research lab and an applied AI care platform, treating over 1 million members directly across a broad range of health conditions, and powering the operational systems that care for millions more.
V’s vision for Sword began when he witnessed firsthand the gap between what society needs from its healthcare system and what a healthcare model constrained by human capacity can deliver. He came to believe that the next era of healthcare would have to be built on new foundations, and that AI would be the technology that made it possible.
He established the theoretical groundwork during his PhD in Electrical Engineering, focused on how AI could extend the reach of human clinicians. After completing his doctorate, he founded Sword to bring that work into practice at global scale.
This impact is built upon a foundation of rigorous scientific research. V holds more than 50 patents and has authored more than 170 peer-reviewed publications spanning sensor fusion, artificial intelligence, and clinical rehabilitation.
His work is guided by a strong conviction that healthcare is the industry where AI can do the most good, and Sword is leading that generation of work.

speakers.name: Virginia Pigato
speakers.bio: Virginia is an Investor at Vento, an early-stage venture fund backed by Exor and the most active early-stage private investor in Italy. She was previously at Techstars and Plug and Play Ventures, where she focused on early-stage investing across robotics, aerospace and consumer electronics.

speakers.name: Vittorio Colao
speakers.bio: Vittorio Colao is Vice Chairman EMEA and Board member of General Atlantic, non-Executive Director of Verizon, and Executive Trustee of Bocconi University. He chaired the Remuneration Committee of Unilever PLC (2015-2021).  He was Minister for Technology Innovation and Digital transition and Delegate authority for Space for the Italian Government with PM Draghi (2021-2022).  In 2024 Vittorio contributed to the Draghi Report ‘The Future of Competitiveness in Europe’.  In 2020 he chaired Italy’s Post Covid recovery committee for Prime Minister Conte.  He was CEO of Vodafone Group (2008-2018). He holds an MBA from Harvard Business School. Received an Honorary Degree, Doctor of Law, at Bath University (2024). Received the Alumni Achievement Award from Harvard Business School (2025). He is a reserve officer of the Italian Carabinieri.

speakers.name: Walter Renna
speakers.bio:
Walter Renna is Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Executive Committee of Fastweb + Vodafone since January 2025.

Renna joined Fastweb in 2008 with responsibilities in strategies, business plan and M&A where he contributed to strategic projects such as the expansion of the fibre access network. Before becoming Chief Product Officer in December 2020, he had held the role of Chief Operating Officer being responsible for long-term business sustainability and growth as well as operational efficiency improvement. He became CEO of Fastweb in 2023. Prior to this, he had a career in KPMG advisory supporting M&A across different industries such as Fashion, Luxury, Publishing and Automotive for leading companies.

Born in 1982, Walter Renna graduated in Economics from the University of Bologna and holds a Master's degree at Bocconi University.

speakers.name: Yoram Wijngaarde
speakers.bio:
Founder of Dealroom.co which was launched in 2014 to provide intelligence
about the world’s most promising startups and ecosystems. Before founding
Dealroom, Yoram was an investment banker at Lehman Brothers, Nomura
Securities and NOAH Advisors in New York and London. Yoram has a cum laude
Master’s degree in Economics from the University of Amsterdam.

speakers.name: Zanny Minton Beddoes
speakers.bio: Zanny Minton Beddoes is the Editor-in-Chief of The Economist. She is a renowned global economics expert, sought-after for her authoritative perspectives on the world economy. She previously worked at the IMF, and as an adviser to the Minister of Finance in Poland.

speakers.name: Zhaopeng Chen
speakers.bio:
He has built the Munich-based company into
a global tech-leader, a pioneer in intelligent
robotic solutions.
Zhaopeng earned his doctorate at the German
Aerospace Center (DLR). As Deputy Director at
the DLR’s Modular Dexterous Robotics Laboratory
(MODEX), he conducted pioneering research.
Zhaopeng developed a widely acclaimed
dexterous robotic hand, regarded as one of the
most sensitive robotic hands, and a milestone
for robotics research.
In 2018 he founded Agile Robots as a spin-off
from the DLR, with the idea to apply world-class
research to real-world manufacturing. Over eight
years Zhaopeng has built a team of more than
2,500 robotics enthusiasts with diverse scientific
and technical backgrounds from all over the world.
From Agile Robots headquarters in Munich, Zhaopeng
oversees Agile Robots growth- The company has
installed over 20,000 robotics solutions worldwide
and is pushing technology and manufacturing
forward - with the development of AI-driven smart
factories.
